pmid:27075904.finding: Eating >=2.8 servings/day of low-to-moderate-pesticide fruit and vegetables was linked to 169% higher total sperm count; high-pesticide produce was not.

pmid:31591650.authors: Williams EA, Parker M, Robinson A, et al.
pmid:31591650.title: A randomized placebo-controlled trial to investigate the effect of lactolycopene on semen quality in healthy males
pmid:31591650.finding: 14 mg/day lactolycopene for 12 weeks improved fast progressive motility and morphology; the primary endpoint was not significant.

pmid:28646871.authors: Ricci E, Viganò P, Cipriani S, et al.
pmid:28646871.title: Coffee and caffeine intake and male infertility: a systematic review
pmid:28646871.finding: Caffeine from coffee and tea was mostly unrelated to semen parameters; caffeinated soft drinks looked harmful; DNA-damage findings inconsistent.

pmid:18650557.authors: Chavarro JE, Toth TL, Sadio SM, et al.
pmid:18650557.title: Soy food and isoflavone intake in relation to semen quality parameters among men from an infertility clinic
pmid:18650557.finding: Men in the highest soy-food category had 41 million/mL lower sperm concentration; no link to motility or morphology.

pmid:26097060.authors: Mínguez-Alarcón L, Afeiche MC, Chiu YH, et al.
pmid:26097060.title: Male soy food intake was not associated with in vitro fertilization outcomes among couples attending a fertility center
pmid:26097060.finding: Male partners' soy intake was unrelated to fertilization, embryo quality or live birth in IVF.

pmid:31116515.authors: Falsig AL, Gleerup CS, Knudsen UB
pmid:31116515.title: The influence of omega-3 fatty acids on semen quality markers: a systematic PRISMA review
pmid:31116515.finding: 14 of 16 studies found omega-3 intake or supplements associated with improvement in at least one semen marker; studies too heterogeneous to pool.

pmid:31951274.authors: Jensen TK, Priskorn L, Holmboe SA, et al.
pmid:31951274.title: Associations of Fish Oil Supplement Use With Testicular Function in Young Men
pmid:31951274.finding: Young men using fish oil supplements on >=60 days had 0.64 mL more semen volume, larger testes and lower FSH and LH.

pmid:27792396.authors: Martínez-Soto JC, Domingo JC, Cordobilla B, et al.
pmid:27792396.title: Dietary supplementation with docosahexaenoic acid (DHA) improves seminal antioxidant status and decreases sperm DNA fragmentation
pmid:27792396.finding: 1.5 g/day DHA for 10 weeks improved seminal antioxidant status and lowered sperm DNA fragmentation, without changing standard parameters.

pmid:30866036.authors: Smits RM, Mackenzie-Proctor R, Yazdani A, et al.
pmid:30866036.title: Antioxidants for male subfertility
pmid:30866036.finding: Cochrane 2019: live birth OR 1.79 (7 RCTs, 750 men, low-quality evidence); no significant benefit once high-risk-of-bias trials were removed (Peto OR 1.38, 0.89-2.16).

pmid:32111479.authors: Steiner AZ, Hansen KR, Barnhart KT, et al.
pmid:32111479.title: The effect of antioxidants on male factor infertility: the Males, Antioxidants, and Infertility (MOXI) randomized clinical trial
pmid:32111479.finding: MOXI: a 7-ingredient antioxidant for 3-6 months did not improve semen parameters or DNA fragmentation; live birth 15% vs 24% placebo.

pmid:15932912.authors: Greco E, Romano S, Iacobelli M, et al.
pmid:15932912.title: ICSI in cases of sperm DNA damage: beneficial effect of oral antioxidant treatment
pmid:15932912.finding: 1 g vitamin C + 1 g vitamin E daily for 2 months lowered SDF in 76% of men; the next ICSI had 48.2% vs 6.9% pregnancy (uncontrolled before-after).

pmid:17425820.authors: Ménézo YJ, Hazout A, Panteix G, et al.
pmid:17425820.title: Antioxidants to reduce sperm DNA fragmentation: an unexpected adverse effect
pmid:17425820.finding: 90 days of antioxidant vitamins with zinc and selenium lowered DFI by 19% but raised sperm decondensation by 23%.

pmid:40015627.authors: Moazamian A, Hug E, Villeneuve P, et al.
pmid:40015627.title: The dual nature of micronutrients on fertility: too much of a good thing?
pmid:40015627.finding: In healthy mice, high doses of vitamin C, zinc, folate or carnitine disturbed redox balance and damaged sperm DNA; high carnitine cut pregnancy rates, but helped oxidatively stressed mice.

pmid:30298673.authors: Stenqvist A, Oleszczuk K, Leijonhufvud I, et al.
pmid:30298673.title: Impact of antioxidant treatment on DNA fragmentation index: a double-blind placebo-controlled randomized trial
pmid:30298673.finding: Six months of combined antioxidants did not lower DNA fragmentation index in men with DFI >=25%.

pmid:17550489.authors: Tremellen K, Miari G, Froiland D, et al.
pmid:17550489.title: A randomised control trial examining the effect of an antioxidant (Menevit) on pregnancy outcome during IVF-ICSI treatment
pmid:17550489.journal: Aust N Z J Obstet Gynaecol
pmid:17550489.finding: Menevit for 3 months before IVF-ICSI: viable pregnancy 38.5% vs 16% per transferred embryo; embryo quality unchanged.

pmid:32330373.authors: Kopets R, Kuibida I, Chernyavska I, et al.
pmid:32330373.title: Dietary supplementation with a novel l-carnitine multi-micronutrient in idiopathic male subfertility involving oligo-, astheno-, teratozoospermia: A randomized clinical study
pmid:32330373.finding: An L-carnitine multi-micronutrient for 6 months raised the share of normal semen analyses (69% vs 22%) and spontaneous pregnancies.

pmid:23912751.authors: Lafuente R, González-Comadrán M, Solà I, et al.
pmid:23912751.title: Coenzyme Q10 and male infertility: a meta-analysis
pmid:23912751.finding: CoQ10 raised sperm concentration and motility, but there was no evidence for higher pregnancy or live birth.

pmid:18395716.authors: Balercia G, Buldreghini E, Vignini A, et al.
pmid:18395716.title: Coenzyme Q10 treatment in infertile men with idiopathic asthenozoospermia: a placebo-controlled, double-blind randomized trial
pmid:18395716.finding: CoQ10 200 mg/day for 6 months increased seminal CoQ10 and motility in idiopathic asthenozoospermia.

pmid:16110353.authors: Comhaire FH, El Garem Y, Mahmoud A, et al.
pmid:16110353.title: Combined conventional/antioxidant "Astaxanthin" treatment for male infertility: a double blind, randomized trial
pmid:16110353.finding: Astaxanthin 16 mg/day for 3 months lowered seminal ROS; pregnancy 54.5% vs 10.5% in a very small trial.

pmid:35128424.authors: Khaw SC, Wong ZZ, Anderson R, et al.
pmid:35128424.title: l-carnitine and l-acetylcarnitine supplementation for idiopathic male infertility
pmid:35128424.finding: Carnitines improved total and progressive motility and morphology, with no demonstrable effect on clinical pregnancy.

pmid:30462179.authors: Salas-Huetos A, Rosique-Esteban N, Becerra-Tomás N, et al.
pmid:30462179.title: The Effect of Nutrients and Dietary Supplements on Sperm Quality Parameters: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis of Randomized Clinical Trials
pmid:30462179.finding: Selenium, zinc, omega-3, CoQ10 and carnitines produced modest improvements in sperm parameters; fertility outcomes not assessed.

pmid:30771790.authors: Jannatifar R, Parivar K, Roodbari NH, et al.
pmid:30771790.title: Effects of N-acetyl-cysteine supplementation on sperm quality, chromatin integrity and level of oxidative stress in infertile men
pmid:30771790.finding: NAC 600 mg/day for 3 months lowered SDF and protamine deficiency and improved count and motility (uncontrolled before-after).

pmid:29126319.authors: Blomberg Jensen M, Lawaetz JG, Petersen JH, et al.
pmid:29126319.title: Effects of Vitamin D Supplementation on Semen Quality, Reproductive Hormones, and Live Birth Rate: A Randomized Clinical Trial
pmid:29126319.finding: Vitamin D (300,000 IU then 1400 IU/day) plus calcium for 150 days did not improve semen quality in vitamin-D-insufficient infertile men.

pmid:28865546.authors: Esteves SC, Roque M, Bradley CK, et al.
pmid:28865546.title: Reproductive outcomes of testicular versus ejaculated sperm for intracytoplasmic sperm injection among men with high levels of DNA fragmentation in semen: systematic review and meta-analysis
pmid:28865546.finding: Testicular sperm had 24.6 points lower SDF than ejaculated sperm; ICSI with testicular sperm gave higher pregnancy and live birth and fewer miscarriages in high-SDF men.

pmid:31692293.authors: Esteves SC, Santi D, Simoni M
pmid:31692293.title: An update on clinical and surgical interventions to reduce sperm DNA fragmentation in infertile men
pmid:31692293.finding: Best evidence for lowering SDF is varicocele repair; antioxidants and lifestyle change may lower SDF but their effect on pregnancy is unclear.

pmid:24681577.authors: Afeiche MC, Williams PL, Gaskins AJ, et al.
pmid:24681577.title: Meat intake and reproductive parameters among young men.
pmid:24681577.finding: Processed red meat was inversely related to total sperm count (top vs bottom quartile -78 million, P-trend 0.01), driven by lower ejaculate volume; unprocessed red meat, poultry and fish were not related to any semen parameter.

pmid:35565922.authors: Liu YS, Zhang YX, Wang XB, et al.
pmid:35565922.title: Associations between Meat and Vegetable Intake, Cooking Methods, and Asthenozoospermia: A Hospital-Based Case-Control Study in China.
pmid:35565922.finding: Highest vs lowest tertile of unprocessed meat intake had lower odds of asthenozoospermia (OR 0.61) and total meat OR 0.56; processed meat raised the odds (OR 1.44) and stir-frying meat was associated with higher risk (OR 1.58).

pmid:29193350.authors: Alizadeh F, Javadi M, Karami AA, et al.
pmid:29193350.title: Curcumin nanomicelle improves semen parameters, oxidative stress, inflammatory biomarkers, and reproductive hormones in infertile men: A randomized clinical trial.
pmid:29193350.finding: 80 mg/day curcumin nanomicelle for 10 weeks raised sperm count, concentration and motility and improved TAC, MDA, CRP and TNF-a versus placebo; single small Iranian trial, no pregnancy or DNA-fragmentation outcomes.

pmid:21337449.title: Can curcumin provide an ideal contraceptive?
pmid:21337449.finding: Curcumin added to human and mouse sperm caused concentration-dependent loss of forward motility, capacitation and fertilisation in vitro, and intravaginal curcumin reduced fertility in mice.

pmid:34755901.authors: Sadraei MR, Tavalaee M, Forouzanfar M, et al.
pmid:34755901.title: Effect of curcumin, and nano-curcumin on sperm function in varicocele rat model.
pmid:34755901.finding: In varicocele rats, oral curcumin and nano-curcumin improved sperm concentration, motility, lipid peroxidation and DNA damage.

pmid:33861392.authors: Santonastaso M, Mottola F, Iovine C, et al.
pmid:33861392.title: Protective Effects of Curcumin on the Outcome of Cryopreservation in Human Sperm.
pmid:33861392.finding: Adding 20 uM curcumin to freezing medium improved post-thaw motility and lowered ROS and DNA fragmentation in human sperm (in vitro, cryopreservation only).

pmid:28295950.authors: Jiang XP, Tang JY, Xu Z, et al.
pmid:28295950.title: Sulforaphane attenuates di-N-butylphthalate-induced reproductive damage in pubertal mice: Involvement of the Nrf2-antioxidant system.
pmid:28295950.finding: Sulforaphane attenuated phthalate (DBP)-induced falls in sperm count, motility and testosterone in pubertal mice via Nrf2.

pmid:31004475.authors: Mu Y, Yin TL, Huang XX, et al.
pmid:31004475.title: Sulforaphane ameliorates high-fat diet-induced spermatogenic deficiency in mice†.
pmid:31004475.finding: Sulforaphane injections reversed high-fat-diet-induced spermatogenic impairment in mice and, in vitro, protected mouse and human sperm motility from palmitic acid via AMPK-dependent ER-stress relief.

pmid:33248050.authors: Valipour J, Nashtaei MS, Khosravizadeh Z, et al.
pmid:33248050.title: Effect of sulforaphane on apoptosis, reactive oxygen species and lipids peroxidation of human sperm during cryopreservation.
pmid:33248050.finding: Adding 5 µM sulforaphane to human sperm before freezing improved post-thaw viability, motility and morphology and lowered ROS and lipid peroxidation.

pmid:24801392.authors: Wang Y, Zhang Z, Guo W, et al.
pmid:24801392.title: Sulforaphane reduction of testicular apoptotic cell death in diabetic mice is associated with the upregulation of Nrf2 expression and function.
pmid:24801392.finding: In diabetic mice, 4 months of sulforaphane prevented testicular cell death, oxidative damage and inflammation while up-regulating testicular Nrf2.

pmid:25275520.authors: Fedder MD, Jakobsen HB, Giversen I, et al.
pmid:25275520.title: An extract of pomegranate fruit and galangal rhizome increases the numbers of motile sperm: a prospective, randomised, controlled, double-blinded trial.
pmid:25275520.finding: Pomegranate extract plus galangal tablets for 3 months increased total motile sperm by 62%, vs 20% on placebo.

pmid:33322606.authors: Illiano E, Trama F, Zucchi A, et al.
pmid:33322606.title: Resveratrol-Based Multivitamin Supplement Increases Sperm Concentration and Motility in Idiopathic Male Infertility: A Pilot Clinical Study.
pmid:33322606.finding: A multivitamin containing 150 mg/day resveratrol was followed by higher sperm motility (48% to 59%) and concentration after 3-6 months.

pmid:36149528.authors: Furini C, Spaggiari G, Simoni M, et al.
pmid:36149528.title: Ketogenic state improves testosterone serum levels-results from a systematic review and meta-analysis.
pmid:36149528.finding: Ketogenic diets raised total testosterone (by ~6.75 nmol/L with very-low-calorie KD, ~1 nmol/L with normocaloric KD), proportional to weight loss and age.

pmid:35223950.authors: Liu CY, Chang TC, Lin SH, et al.
pmid:35223950.title: Is a Ketogenic Diet Superior to a High-Fat, High-Cholesterol Diet Regarding Testicular Function and Spermatogenesis?
pmid:35223950.finding: In obese mice, switching from a high-fat high-cholesterol diet to an MCT-based ketogenic diet for 8 weeks lowered testicular lipid peroxidation and restored semen quality.

pmid:33741447.title: Low-fat diets and testosterone in men: Systematic review and meta-analysis of intervention studies.
pmid:33741447.finding: Low-fat diets lowered total testosterone (SMD -0.38) and free testosterone (SMD -0.37) vs higher-fat diets.

pmid:3090956.title: Effects of Ramadhan fast on male fertility.
pmid:3090956.finding: Small study: Ramadan did not harm semen in healthy men; LH and semen volume fell after the fast while sperm count rose during it.

pmid:1904451.authors: Cameron JL, Weltzin TE, McConaha C, et al.
pmid:1904451.title: Slowing of pulsatile luteinizing hormone secretion in men after forty-eight hours of fasting.
pmid:1904451.finding: 48 h of fasting cut mean LH from 2.94 to 1.07 IU/L and halved LH pulse frequency, and lowered FSH and testosterone, without a rise in cortisol.

pmid:35684143.authors: Cienfuegos S, Corapi S, Gabel K, et al.
pmid:35684143.title: Effect of Intermittent Fasting on Reproductive Hormone Levels in Females and Males: A Review of Human Trials.
pmid:35684143.finding: Review of human trials: IF lowers testosterone/free androgen index and raises SHBG in premenopausal women with obesity, does not change oestrogen or gonadotropins, and lowers testosterone in lean active young men.

pmid:37883941.authors: Engel OJ, Doctory N, Sun B, et al.
pmid:37883941.title: The Effect of Month-Long Daily Fasting on Semen Parameters: A Retrospective Cohort Study.
pmid:37883941.finding: Semen samples produced during Ramadan (and 70 days after) had lower post-gradient progressive motility (30% vs 38%) and lower volume than the same men's samples at other times (retrospective).

pmid:39885870.authors: May KT, Behling J, Sochiera-Plegniere K, et al.
pmid:39885870.title: Fasting for male fertility-a mixed methods study.
pmid:39885870.finding: Three 5-day 500 kcal FMD cycles over 4 months produced no clear differences in semen parameters vs waiting-list controls (pilot, underpowered).

pmid:38781203.authors: Poursalehian M, Mohseni S, Shadman Z, et al.
pmid:38781203.title: Impact of Ramadan fasting on serum levels of major endocrinology hormonal and biochemical parameters in healthy non-athlete adults: A systematic review and meta-analyses.
pmid:38781203.finding: Ramadan fasting did not significantly change testosterone, LH, FSH, prolactin or thyroid hormones in healthy non-athletes; morning cortisol tended to fall.

pmid:38861008.authors: Aerts A, Temmerman A, Vanhie A, et al.
pmid:38861008.title: The Effect of Endurance Exercise on Semen Quality in Male Athletes: A Systematic Review.
pmid:38861008.finding: Endurance exercise can lower semen quality, but changes were usually not clinically relevant; some cyclists and triathletes had more abnormal morphology or DNA fragmentation.

pmid:37052052.title: Hungry runners - low energy availability in male endurance athletes and its impact on performance and testosterone: mini-review.
pmid:37052052.finding: Low energy availability is common in male endurance athletes and correlates with lower testosterone, bone density and resting metabolic rate.

pmid:19092301.title: Effects of endurance exercise on the reproductive system of men: the "exercise-hypogonadal male condition".
pmid:19092301.finding: Describes the exercise-hypogonadal male condition as limited to men with years of chronic endurance training and not highly prevalent.

pmid:28195945.authors: Hackney AC, Lane AR, Register-Mihalik J, et al.
pmid:28195945.title: Endurance Exercise Training and Male Sexual Libido.
pmid:28195945.finding: Men with the highest training intensity and duration had greater odds of low libido than those training least.

pmid:32082255.title: Hypogonadism in Exercising Males: Dysfunction or Adaptive-Regulatory Adjustment?
pmid:32082255.finding: Proposes several forms of exercise-related male hypogonadism, some transient and linked to low energy availability or overtraining, others possibly an adaptive readjustment.

pmid:37752011.authors: Mountjoy M, Ackerman KE, Bailey DM, et al.
pmid:37752011.title: 2023 International Olympic Committee's (IOC) consensus statement on Relative Energy Deficiency in Sport (REDs).
pmid:37752011.finding: IOC 2023 consensus on Relative Energy Deficiency in Sport (REDs), covering reproductive suppression from low energy availability in both sexes.

pmid:28295487.authors: Vaamonde D, Algar-Santacruz C, Abbasi A, et al.
pmid:28295487.title: Sperm DNA fragmentation as a result of ultra-endurance exercise training in male athletes.
pmid:28295487.finding: Elite triathletes in training had high sperm DNA fragmentation (mean 20.4%) and raised round cells.

pmid:17509584.authors: Agarwal A, Deepinder F, Cocuzza M, et al.
pmid:17509584.title: Effect of vaginal lubricants on sperm motility and chromatin integrity: a prospective comparative study.
pmid:17509584.finding: In vitro, FemGlide, Replens and Astroglide reduced progressive motility and FemGlide and K-Y Jelly raised DNA fragmentation (SCSA), whereas Pre-Seed did not differ from culture medium.

pmid:23490168.authors: Agarwal A, Malvezzi H, Sharma R
pmid:23490168.title: Effect of an isotonic lubricant on sperm collection and sperm quality.
pmid:23490168.finding: Using Pre-Seed during masturbation for semen collection did not change motility, viability, ROS, antioxidant capacity or DNA damage.

pmid:9886513.authors: Anderson L, Lewis SE, McClure N
pmid:9886513.title: The effects of coital lubricants on sperm motility in vitro.
pmid:9886513.finding: K-Y jelly, olive oil and saliva (but not baby oil) significantly reduced sperm motility in vitro at 12.5%; olive oil and saliva still did at 6.25%.

pmid:27268162.authors: Bach CC, Vested A, Jørgensen KT, et al.
pmid:27268162.title: Perfluoroalkyl and polyfluoroalkyl substances and measures of human fertility: a systematic review.
pmid:27268162.finding: Little consistent evidence that PFAS affect semen quality or hormones in men; associations with longer time to pregnancy appear in parous women and are most likely not causal.

pmid:42570390.authors: Di Nisio A, López-Gil JF, Pizzol D, et al.
pmid:42570390.title: Associations between per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances and semen parameters: An updated systematic review and meta-analysis.
pmid:42570390.finding: PFAS were weakly associated with lower progressive motility (r = -0.058) and more sperm DNA fragmentation (r = 0.141), with little association with standard counts.

pmid:38044638.authors: Gumerova E, Rimmer MP, Gellatly SA
pmid:38044638.title: Do sperm and lubricants gel well with each other? A systematic review.
pmid:38044638.finding: Systematic review: only 2 of 24 studies were in vivo; methodological variation and absent pregnancy outcomes prevent an evidence-based "sperm-safe" lubricant guideline.

pmid:40711011.authors: Guo Y, Rong M, Fan Y, et al.
pmid:40711011.title: The Presence of Microplastics in Human Semen and Their Associations with Semen Quality.
pmid:40711011.finding: Laser-direct infrared found microplastics in 34 of 45 semen samples; men with PET particles had borderline lower progressive motility (20.6% vs 34.9%, p=0.056) and no difference in concentration or count.

pmid:19590684.authors: Joensen UN, Bossi R, Leffers H, et al.
pmid:19590684.title: Do perfluoroalkyl compounds impair human semen quality?
pmid:19590684.finding: Men with high combined PFOS+PFOA had fewer morphologically normal sperm (6.2 vs 15.5 million per ejaculate).

pmid:38802004.authors: Li N, Yang H, Dong Y, et al.
pmid:38802004.title: Prevalence and implications of microplastic contaminants in general human seminal fluid: A Raman spectroscopic study.
pmid:38802004.finding: Raman found about 2 microplastic particles per semen sample in all 40 men (mostly polystyrene); PVC-containing samples had lower progressive motility than polystyrene-containing ones.

pmid:25127343.authors: Louis GM, Chen Z, Schisterman EF, et al.
pmid:25127343.title: Perfluorochemicals and human semen quality: the LIFE study.
pmid:25127343.finding: Several PFAS were associated with some semen endpoints, but in varying directions; strongest signals were for PFOSA and sperm head morphology.

pmid:31086364.title: Vaginal lubricants in the couple trying-to-conceive: Assessing healthcare professional recommendations and effect on in vitro sperm function.
pmid:31086364.n: 32 clinician survey responses plus lab testing
pmid:31086364.finding: Aquagel cut progressive motility to 49% of control within 10 min even at 5%, while a sperm-safe lubricant (Pre) had no effect; clinicians' advice was inconsistent.

pmid:29543376.authors: McInerney KA, Hahn KA, Hatch EE, et al.
pmid:29543376.title: Lubricant use during intercourse and time to pregnancy: a prospective cohort study.
pmid:29543376.finding: No lubricant type was associated with lower fecundability (water-based FR 1.02; "fertility-friendly" 1.01; oil-based 1.23; silicone 1.27).

pmid:24717914.title: Effect of vaginal lubricants on natural fertility.
pmid:24717914.finding: In vitro, many lubricants are sperm-toxic while "sperm-friendly" ones are not, yet cohort data show no effect on fecundity; an RCT is needed.

pmid:37532047.authors: Montano L, Giorgini E, Notarstefano V, et al.
pmid:37532047.title: Raman Microspectroscopy evidence of microplastics in human semen.
pmid:37532047.finding: Raman microspectroscopy found 16 microplastic fragments (2-6 um) in 6 of 10 semen samples from a polluted area of southern Italy.

pmid:24390681.authors: Mowat A, Newton C, Boothroyd C, et al.
pmid:24390681.title: The effects of vaginal lubricants on sperm function: an in vitro analysis.
pmid:24390681.finding: Of nine lubricants tested in vitro, Pre-Seed preserved motility (86%) and vitality (92%) best and Conceive Plus was second; none affected DNA fragmentation over 30 min.

pmid:29722171.authors: Samarasinghe SVAC, Krishnan K, Naidu R, et al.
pmid:29722171.title: Parabens generate reactive oxygen species in human spermatozoa.
pmid:29722171.finding: Parabens at concentrations found in vaginal lubricants generated mitochondrial ROS and oxidative DNA adducts and reduced sperm motility and viability in vitro.

pmid:22449571.authors: Specht IO, Hougaard KS, Spanò M, et al.
pmid:22449571.title: Sperm DNA integrity in relation to exposure to environmental perfluoroalkyl substances - a study of spouses of pregnant women in three geographical regions.
pmid:22449571.finding: No consistent association between serum PFAS and sperm DNA fragmentation (SCSA), apoptosis markers or reproductive hormones; only a slight TUNEL rise with PFOA in Greenland.

pmid:22914390.authors: Steiner AZ, Long DL, Tanner C, et al.
pmid:22914390.title: Effect of vaginal lubricants on natural fertility.
pmid:22914390.finding: Lubricant use in the fertile window did not reduce fecundability (fecundability ratio 1.05, 95% CI 0.59-1.85).

pmid:35369832.authors: Tomlinson J, Pooley K, Tomlinson M
pmid:35369832.title: Sperm toxicity testing on lubricant gels: should we be recommending 'fertility-friendly' specialist products?
pmid:35369832.finding: All gels reduced motility in vitro; products marketed as sperm-friendly (FertilSafe Plus) performed best, pleasure lubricants worst, and saliva was worse still.

pmid:6890474.authors: Tulandi T, Plouffe L, McInnes RA
pmid:6890474.title: Effect of saliva on sperm motility and activity.
pmid:6890474.finding: Saliva reduced sperm motility and progression in vitro, even at low concentrations.

pmid:36396760.authors: Wang H, Wei K, Wu Z, et al.
pmid:36396760.title: Association between per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances and semen quality.
pmid:36396760.finding: PFOA and PFNA were associated with lower progressive sperm motility; other semen parameters were largely unaffected.

pmid:36948312.authors: Zhao Q, Zhu L, Weng J, et al.
pmid:36948312.title: Detection and characterization of microplastics in the human testis and semen.
pmid:36948312.finding: Py-GC/MS and laser-direct infrared found microplastics in testis (11.6 particles/g) and semen (0.23 particles/mL), mostly 20-100 um.

pmid:24529582.authors: Akasheh G, Sirati L, Noshad Kamran AR, et al.
pmid:24529582.title: Comparison of the effect of sertraline with behavioral therapy on semen parameters in men with primary premature ejaculation.
pmid:24529582.finding: Sertraline 50 mg/day for 3 months (vs behavioural therapy) lowered sperm concentration and normal morphology and raised sperm DNA fragmentation.

pmid:17299062.authors: Amory JK, Wang C, Swerdloff RS, et al.
pmid:17299062.title: The effect of 5alpha-reductase inhibition with dutasteride and finasteride on semen parameters and serum hormones in healthy men.
pmid:17299062.finding: Dutasteride 0.5 mg and finasteride 5 mg cut total sperm count by 28.6% and 34.3% at 26 weeks, lowered volume and motility, with largely reversible effects after stopping.

pmid:30864530.authors: Banerjee A, Scarpa M, Pathak S, et al.
pmid:30864530.title: Inflammatory Bowel Disease Therapies Adversely Affect Fertility in Men- A Systematic Review and Meta-analysis.
pmid:30864530.journal: Endocr Metab Immune Disord Drug Targets
pmid:30864530.finding: Sulphasalazine-treated men had lower sperm counts and motility and more oligospermia than mesalazine-treated men; biologics appeared safe.

pmid:25702934.authors: Bawor M, Bami H, Dennis BB, et al.
pmid:25702934.title: Testosterone suppression in opioid users: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
pmid:25702934.finding: Regular opioid use (including methadone) lowered testosterone in men by about 165 ng/dL versus controls; no effect seen in women.

pmid:31542895.title: Effect of antidepressant medications on semen parameters and male fertility.
pmid:31542895.finding: SSRIs, especially fluoxetine, are linked to lower sperm concentration and motility and higher DNA fragmentation in human and animal studies; effects appear reversible; data on other antidepressants are sparse.

pmid:28277353.authors: Eck LK, Jensen TB, Mastrogiannis D, et al.
pmid:28277353.title: Risk of Adverse Pregnancy Outcome After Paternal Exposure to Methotrexate Within 90 Days Before Pregnancy.
pmid:28277353.finding: Paternal methotrexate within 90 days before conception was not associated with major malformations (aOR 1.01), stillbirth or preterm birth.

pmid:29778387.authors: Evans-Hoeker EA, Eisenberg E, Diamond MP, et al.
pmid:29778387.title: Major depression, antidepressant use, and male and female fertility.
pmid:29778387.n: 1650 women and 1608 men in infertility trials
pmid:29778387.finding: Active major depression in the male partner lowered conception; maternal antidepressant use (n=90) was associated with first-trimester pregnancy loss.

pmid:16952675.title: Effects of acute treatment with tamsulosin versus alfuzosin on ejaculatory function in normal volunteers.
pmid:16952675.finding: Tamsulosin 0.8 mg daily lowered ejaculate volume by 2.4 mL and caused anejaculation in 35% of men; alfuzosin and placebo did not.

pmid:21776003.authors: Koyuncu H, Serefoglu EC, Yencilek E, et al.
pmid:21776003.title: Escitalopram treatment for premature ejaculation has a negative effect on semen parameters.
pmid:21776003.finding: Escitalopram 10 mg daily for 12 weeks lowered sperm concentration, motility and morphology.

pmid:6148293.authors: O'Moráin C, Smethurst P, Doré CJ, et al.
pmid:6148293.title: Reversible male infertility due to sulphasalazine: studies in man and rat.
pmid:6148293.n: men with IBD plus rat studies
pmid:6148293.finding: Sulphasalazine caused oligospermia, poor motility and abnormal forms that reversed on withdrawal (15 pregnancies at a median 2.5 months); the sulphapyridine moiety was responsible in rats.

pmid:10492183.authors: Overstreet JW, Fuh VL, Gould J, et al.
pmid:10492183.title: Chronic treatment with finasteride daily does not affect spermatogenesis or semen production in young men.
pmid:10492183.finding: Finasteride 1 mg daily for 48 weeks did not affect sperm concentration, count, motility or morphology versus placebo.

pmid:32743663.authors: Perez-Garcia LF, Dolhain RJEM, Vorstenbosch S, et al.
pmid:32743663.title: The effect of paternal exposure to immunosuppressive drugs on sexual function, reproductive hormones, fertility, pregnancy and offspring outcomes: a systematic review.
pmid:32743663.finding: Clear negative effects on sperm for sulfasalazine and cyclophosphamide; dubious effects for methotrexate, colchicine and sirolimus; no large negative offspring effects of paternal immunosuppressants reported.

pmid:37263756.authors: Perez-Garcia LF, Röder E, Krijthe BP, et al.
pmid:37263756.title: Is methotrexate safe for men with an immune-mediated inflammatory disease and an active desire to become a father? Results of a prospective cohort study (iFAME-MTX).
pmid:37263756.finding: Semen parameters and sperm DNA fragmentation did not change after starting low-dose methotrexate and matched healthy controls; methotrexate barely accumulated in sperm.

pmid:18804223.title: Sperm DNA damage and semen quality impairment after treatment with selective serotonin reuptake inhibitors detected using semen analysis and sperm chromatin structure assay.
pmid:18804223.finding: Reported lower sperm count and motility and higher DNA denaturation with SSRIs; the journal issued an Expression of Concern in 2023, so this paper should not be relied on.

pmid:23082785.title: Investigation of ejaculatory disorder by silodosin in the treatment of prostatic hyperplasia.
pmid:23082785.finding: Among sexually active men on silodosin, 95% reported ejaculatory disorder.

pmid:24012200.authors: Samplaski MK, Lo K, Grober E, et al.
pmid:24012200.title: Finasteride use in the male infertility population: effects on semen and hormone parameters.
pmid:24012200.finding: In men presenting with infertility while on finasteride (mean 1 mg/day), sperm counts rose on average 11.6-fold after stopping; 57% of severely oligospermic men rose above 15 million/mL.

pmid:30676405.authors: Sylvester C, Menke M, Gopalan P
pmid:30676405.title: Selective Serotonin Reuptake Inhibitors and Fertility: Considerations for Couples Trying to Conceive.
pmid:30676405.finding: Insufficient evidence that SSRIs reduce female fertility or IVF outcomes; six of seven mostly poor-quality male studies found adverse effects on semen.

pmid:19515367.authors: Tanrikut C, Feldman AS, Altemus M, et al.
pmid:19515367.title: Adverse effect of paroxetine on sperm.
pmid:19515367.finding: Five weeks of paroxetine raised mean sperm DNA fragmentation from 13.8% to 30.3% (TUNEL); abnormal fragmentation rose from 9.7% to 50% of men (OR 9.3) without changes in standard semen parameters.

pmid:6114897.authors: Toovey S, Hudson E, Hendry WF, et al.
pmid:6114897.title: Sulphasalazine and male infertility: reversibility and possible mechanism.
pmid:6114897.finding: Sulphasalazine 2-4 g/day caused gross semen abnormalities in 18 men treated over 2 months; quality recovered after withdrawal and 10 pregnancies followed.

pmid:35144505.authors: Yland JJ, McKinnon CJ, Hatch EE, et al.
pmid:35144505.title: A Prospective Study of Male Depression, Psychotropic Medication Use, and Fecundability.
pmid:35144505.finding: Male depression history was weakly associated with lower fecundability (FR 0.89, CI crossing 1); current psychotropic medication use statistically mediated 44% of the depressive-symptom association.

pmid:32654822.authors: Practice Committees of the American Society for Reproductive Medicine and the Society for Assisted Reproductive Technology
pmid:32654822.title: Intracytoplasmic sperm injection (ICSI) for non-male factor indications: a committee opinion
pmid:32654822.finding: ASRM/SART committee opinion reviewing when ICSI may or may not benefit couples whose semen meets WHO reference values; routine ICSI for non-male factor is not supported.

pmid:35263457.authors: Aydın Ş, Bulgan Kılıçdağ E, Çağlar Aytaç P, et al.
pmid:35263457.title: Prospective randomized controlled study of a microfluidic chip technology for sperm selection in male infertility patients
pmid:35263457.finding: Single-centre RCT in male-factor ICSI: microfluidic chip vs swim-up gave similar fertilisation and embryo quality but higher live birth (46.8% vs 25%).

pmid:25602996.authors: Boulet SL, Mehta A, Kissin DM, et al.
pmid:25602996.title: Trends in use of and reproductive outcomes associated with intracytoplasmic sperm injection
pmid:25602996.finding: US registry: ICSI use without male factor rose from 15.4% to 66.9% (1996-2012) and, in those cycles, was associated with slightly lower live birth than conventional IVF (36.5% vs 39.2%; aRR 0.95).

pmid:33894833.authors: Dang VQ, Vuong LN, Luu TM, et al.
pmid:33894833.title: Intracytoplasmic sperm injection versus conventional in-vitro fertilisation in couples with infertility in whom the male partner has normal total sperm count and motility: an open-label, randomised controlled trial
pmid:33894833.finding: In couples with normal sperm count and motility, ICSI did not raise live birth over conventional IVF (35% vs 31%; RR 1.11, 95% CI 0.93-1.32); total fertilisation failure was similar (5% vs 6%).

pmid:37747409.authors: ESHRE Add-ons working group; Lundin K, Bentzen JG, Bozdag G, et al.
pmid:37747409.title: Good practice recommendations on add-ons in reproductive medicine
pmid:37747409.finding: ESHRE good practice recommendations on 42 add-ons: none based on high-quality evidence; not recommended include endometrial receptivity tests, immune testing and immunomodulators (Intralipid, IVIG), glucocorticoids, assisted hatching, time-lapse imaging (to improve live birth), intrauterine hCG, intrauterine and intraovarian PRP, mitochondrial replacement, adjuncts during stimulation (growth hormone, DHEA, testosterone), oral antioxidants and ICSI for non-male factor; PGT-A, endometrial scratching, MACS, PICSI and IMSI 'not recommended for routine clinical use'; microfluidics 'can be considered'; hyaluronan in transfer medium 'recommended' (with single embryo transfer).

pmid:42227305.authors: Garg A, Nakhla O, Steeper M, et al.
pmid:42227305.title: Advanced sperm selection techniques for assisted reproduction
pmid:42227305.finding: Cochrane 2026: hyaluronan-selected ICSI may make no or a slight difference to live birth (RR 1.09, 0.97-1.24; low certainty) and probably slightly reduces miscarriage (RR 0.59; moderate); effects of other techniques (MACS, microfluidics, IMSI) unknown due to very low certainty.

sperm:fer-hfea2026.title: Treatment add-ons with limited evidence (HFEA add-ons rating list)
sperm:fer-hfea2026.finding: HFEA traffic-light ratings for 'chances of having a baby' (page reviewed 28 Sep 2026; ratings set by SCAAC): yellow/amber (unclear) for endometrial scratching, hyaluronate-enriched transfer medium and elective freeze-all; grey (insufficient evidence) for assisted hatching, androgens, intralipids, IMSI, intrauterine culture, microbiome testing and SDF-guided treatments; black (no effect) for time-lapse imaging and PICSI; red (no benefit and/or safety concerns) for endometrial receptivity testing, IVIG, steroids, PRP and PGT-A (PGT-A rated green for reducing miscarriage). No green rating for live birth.

sperm:fer-hfea2026sdf.title: Sperm DNA fragmentation: treatment add-on rating
sperm:fer-hfea2026sdf.finding: After SDF testing: antioxidants and sperm selection (DGC/MACS with ICSI or PICSI) rated grey (insufficient evidence) for male factor and recurrent pregnancy loss; testicular sperm (TESE/TESA) with ICSI rated red for male factor (insufficient evidence plus surgical risk). Reviewed 24 Sep 2026.

pmid:41757843.authors: Huong DT, Tam DTM, Hoa NT, et al.
pmid:41757843.title: Comparative Efficacy of Microfluidics and Density Gradient Centrifugation for Sperm Preparation in IVF: A Randomized Controlled Trial
pmid:41757843.finding: Microfluidic preparation lowered sperm DNA fragmentation index more than density gradients, especially with high baseline DFI, but did not improve pregnancy or live birth.

pmid:38700621.title: In cases with raised sperm DNA fragmentation, can sperm selection by magnetic-activated cell sorting or testicular sperm aspiration help improve reproductive outcomes?
pmid:38700621.n: couples with failed IVF and SDF >30%
pmid:38700621.finding: In couples with raised sperm DNA fragmentation, MACS-selected and testicular sperm gave comparable live birth; no control arm without either.

pmid:30712901.authors: Miller D, Pavitt S, Sharma V, et al.
pmid:30712901.title: Physiological, hyaluronan-selected intracytoplasmic sperm injection for infertility treatment (HABSelect): a parallel, two-group, randomised trial
pmid:30712901.finding: HABSelect: hyaluronan-selected sperm (PICSI) did not raise term live birth vs ICSI (27.4% vs 25.2%; OR 1.12, 95% CI 0.95-1.34); miscarriage was a secondary finding.

pmid:25305728.authors: Romany L, Garrido N, Motato Y, et al.
pmid:25305728.title: Removal of annexin V-positive sperm cells for intracytoplasmic sperm injection in ovum donation cycles does not improve reproductive outcome: a controlled and randomized trial in unselected males
pmid:25305728.finding: Removing annexin V-positive sperm by MACS did not improve fertilisation, embryo quality or live birth (48.4% vs 56.4%, NS) in donor-egg ICSI.

pmid:30852746.authors: Ammar O, Houas Z, Mehdi M
pmid:30852746.title: The association between iron, calcium, and oxidative stress in seminal plasma and sperm quality
pmid:30852746.finding: Seminal iron was higher in subfertile men and correlated negatively with sperm motility and normal morphology.

pmid:42101252.authors: Carlomagno F, Tenuta M, Sansone A, et al.
pmid:42101252.title: Iron overload disorders in adults: a comprehensive review of gonadal function, reproductive, and sexual health
pmid:42101252.n: Systematic review: 1201 men, 2134 women with iron overload
pmid:42101252.finding: In iron overload disorders, 47% of men had hypogonadism and over half of those assessed had azoospermia or other sperm abnormalities; early chelation helps prevent but rarely reverses damage.

pmid:12093845.authors: Perera D, Pizzey A, Campbell A, et al.
pmid:12093845.title: Sperm DNA damage in potentially fertile homozygous beta-thalassaemia patients with iron overload
pmid:12093845.finding: Iron-overloaded men (median ferritin 2251 ug/L) had more sperm DNA damage, which rose with later onset of chelation.

pmid:22748101.authors: Agarwal A, Aponte-Mellado A, Premkumar BJ, et al.
pmid:22748101.title: The effects of oxidative stress on female reproduction: a review
pmid:22748101.finding: Narrative review: oxidative stress is implicated in endometriosis, PCOS, unexplained infertility and pregnancy complications; antioxidant evidence is mostly animal/in-vitro and conflicting.

pmid:21220312.authors: Shkolnik K, Tadmor A, Ben-Dor S, et al.
pmid:21220312.title: Reactive oxygen species are indispensable in ovulation
pmid:21220312.journal: Proc Natl Acad Sci U S A
pmid:21220312.finding: In mice, antioxidants injected into the ovarian bursa reduced ovulation and blocked LH-induced cumulus expansion; H2O2 mimicked LH. ROS are an essential pre-ovulatory signal.

pmid:27562289.authors: May-Panloup P, Boucret L, Chao de la Barca JM, et al.
pmid:27562289.title: Ovarian ageing: the role of mitochondria in oocytes and follicles
pmid:27562289.finding: Oocytes are the most mitochondria-rich cells in the body; ageing-related mtDNA instability and impaired mitochondrial biogenesis in oocytes and granulosa cells are closely linked to declining oocyte quality.

pmid:18223651.authors: Cree LM, Samuels DC, de Sousa Lopes SC, et al.
pmid:18223651.title: A reduction of mitochondrial DNA molecules during embryogenesis explains the rapid segregation of genotypes
pmid:18223651.finding: Mouse study: mtDNA is maternally inherited and passes through a genetic bottleneck (partitioning of mtDNA molecules during embryogenesis and germ-cell proliferation) that explains rapid shifts in heteroplasmy between generations.

pmid:24355045.authors: Franasiak JM, Forman EJ, Hong KH, et al.
pmid:24355045.title: The nature of aneuploidy with increasing age of the female partner: a review of 15,169 consecutive trophectoderm biopsies evaluated with comprehensive chromosomal screening
pmid:24355045.finding: Embryo aneuploidy was lowest at ages 26-30 and rose predictably after 26; the chance of having no euploid embryo was 2-6% at ages 26-37, 33% at 42 and 53% at 44.

pmid:31604276.authors: Gruhn JR, Zielinska AP, Shukla V, et al.
pmid:31604276.title: Chromosome errors in human eggs shape natural fertility over reproductive life span
pmid:31604276.finding: Aneuploidy in human eggs follows a U-curve with age; in older women it is driven by centromeric and more extensive loss of sister-chromatid cohesion.

pmid:32049001.authors: Bertoldo MJ, Listijono DR, Ho WJ, et al.
pmid:32049001.title: NAD(+) Repletion Rescues Female Fertility during Reproductive Aging
pmid:32049001.finding: In aged mice, oocyte NAD+ falls with age; the precursor NMN restored oocyte quality, fertility and embryo development. Mouse data only.

pmid:32755581.authors: Miao Y, Cui Z, Gao Q, et al.
pmid:32755581.title: Nicotinamide Mononucleotide Supplementation Reverses the Declining Quality of Maternally Aged Oocytes
pmid:32755581.finding: In naturally aged mice, NMN restored oocyte NAD+, spindle/chromosome structure, fertilization ability and mitochondrial function and lowered ROS. Mouse data only.

pmid:3558758.title: Dynamics of follicular growth in the human: a model from preliminary results
pmid:3558758.finding: Human follicle growth is very long: the ovulatory follicle comes from a cohort of preantral follicles that differentiated about 85 days earlier; it is recruited 15-20 days before ovulation.

pmid:20362973.title: Human ovarian follicular development: from activation of resting follicles to preovulatory maturation
pmid:20362973.finding: Several months are needed for a growing follicle to reach the preantral stage, then about 70 more days to reach 2 mm before cyclic selection.

pmid:16861701.authors: Das S, Chattopadhyay R, Ghosh S, et al.
pmid:16861701.title: Reactive oxygen species level in follicular fluid--embryo quality marker in IVF?
pmid:16861701.finding: Higher follicular fluid ROS and lipid peroxidation were associated with fertilization failure, pronuclear arrest and poor-grade embryos.

pmid:18339123.authors: Tamura H, Takasaki A, Miwa I, et al.
pmid:18339123.title: Oxidative stress impairs oocyte quality and melatonin protects oocytes from free radical damage and improves fertilization rate
pmid:18339123.finding: Follicular 8-OHdG (oxidative DNA damage) was higher where many oocytes degenerated; melatonin 3 mg/day and/or vitamin E 600 mg/day lowered follicular oxidative markers, and melatonin was associated with better fertilization vs the previous failed cycle (not randomized).

pmid:20643402.authors: Meseguer M, Santiso R, Garrido N, et al.
pmid:20643402.title: Effect of sperm DNA fragmentation on pregnancy outcome depends on oocyte quality
pmid:20643402.finding: Sperm DNA fragmentation lowered pregnancy odds when the woman's own (infertile-patient) oocytes were used, but had no significant effect with donor oocytes, implying good oocytes can compensate for sperm DNA damage.

pmid:20663262.authors: Ménézo Y, Dale B, Cohen M
pmid:20663262.title: DNA damage and repair in human oocytes and embryos: a review
pmid:20663262.finding: Early embryos rely on maternally stored DNA-repair transcripts until embryonic genome activation at the 4-8 cell stage; the oocyte must repair DNA damage brought in by sperm.

pmid:24559617.authors: ACOG Committee on Gynecologic Practice; ASRM Practice Committee
pmid:24559617.title: Female age-related fertility decline. Committee Opinion No. 589
pmid:24559617.finding: ACOG/ASRM: female fecundity declines gradually from about age 32 and more rapidly after 37; evaluate after 6 months of trying at >35 and immediately at >40.

pmid:23303572.authors: Murri M, Luque-Ramírez M, Insenser M, et al.
pmid:23303572.title: Circulating markers of oxidative stress and polycystic ovary syndrome (PCOS): a systematic review and meta-analysis
pmid:23303572.finding: Women with PCOS had higher circulating malondialdehyde (+47%), homocysteine (+23%) and ADMA, and about 50% lower glutathione, independent of weight excess.

pmid:28701212.authors: Sanchez AM, Vanni VS, Bartiromo L, et al.
pmid:28701212.title: Is the oocyte quality affected by endometriosis? A review of the literature
pmid:28701212.finding: Systematic review: oocytes from women with endometriosis are more likely to fail in-vitro maturation, show altered morphology and lower mitochondrial content; granulosa cells show more ROS.

pmid:26168799.authors: Hamdan M, Dunselman G, Li TC, et al.
pmid:26168799.title: The impact of endometrioma on IVF/ICSI outcomes: a systematic review and meta-analysis
pmid:26168799.finding: Endometrioma was associated with fewer oocytes retrieved and more cancelled cycles, but similar live birth rates (OR 0.98); surgery before IVF did not improve outcomes.

pmid:19574447.authors: Wang Q, Ratchford AM, Chi MM, et al.
pmid:19574447.title: Maternal diabetes causes mitochondrial dysfunction and meiotic defects in murine oocytes
pmid:19574447.finding: In diabetic mice, oocytes showed abnormal mitochondrial structure and distribution, lower ATP and TCA metabolites, more spindle defects and higher aneuploidy.

pmid:21170514.authors: Whitworth KW, Baird DD, Stene LC, et al.
pmid:21170514.title: Fecundability among women with type 1 and type 2 diabetes in the Norwegian Mother and Child Cohort Study
pmid:21170514.finding: Fecundability odds were lower in women with type 1 diabetes (FOR 0.76) and type 2 diabetes (FOR 0.64), even with regular cycles.

pmid:19223519.authors: Robker RL, Akison LK, Bennett BD, et al.
pmid:19223519.title: Obese women exhibit differences in ovarian metabolites, hormones, and gene expression compared with moderate-weight women
pmid:19223519.finding: Higher BMI was associated with higher follicular fluid insulin, lactate, triglycerides and C-reactive protein: an altered, more inflammatory follicular environment.

pmid:20861227.authors: Wu LL, Dunning KR, Yang X, et al.
pmid:20861227.title: High-fat diet causes lipotoxicity responses in cumulus-oocyte complexes and decreased fertilization rates
pmid:20861227.finding: High-fat-diet obese mice had lipid-laden oocytes with reduced mitochondrial membrane potential, ER stress, cumulus apoptosis and lower fertilization; ER stress markers were also raised in granulosa cells of obese women.

pmid:30941397.authors: Sermondade N, Huberlant S, Bourhis-Lefebvre V, et al.
pmid:30941397.title: Female obesity is negatively associated with live birth rate following IVF: a systematic review and meta-analysis
pmid:30941397.finding: Obese women (BMI >= 30) had lower live birth rates after IVF than normal-weight women (RR 0.85); worse when combined with PCOS.

pmid:1559293.authors: Kiddy DS, Hamilton-Fairley D, Bush A, et al.
pmid:1559293.title: Improvement in endocrine and ovarian function during dietary treatment of obese women with polycystic ovary syndrome
pmid:1559293.finding: Women who lost more than 5% of body weight on a 1000 kcal diet had lower insulin, higher SHBG and 9 of 11 improved reproductive function; those losing less than 5% did not improve.

pmid:27192672.authors: Mutsaerts MA, van Oers AM, Groen H, et al.
pmid:27192672.title: Randomized Trial of a Lifestyle Program in Obese Infertile Women
pmid:27192672.finding: LIFEstyle trial: a 6-month lifestyle program before fertility treatment (mean loss 4.4 kg) did not increase healthy term singleton births at 24 months (27.1% vs 35.2%; RR 0.77).

pmid:28854592.authors: Einarsson S, Bergh C, Friberg B, et al.
pmid:28854592.title: Weight reduction intervention for obese infertile women prior to IVF: a randomized controlled trial
pmid:28854592.finding: Intensive weight loss (12 weeks 880 kcal/day, mean -9.4 kg) before IVF did not change IVF live birth (29.6% vs 27.5%), but more spontaneous conceptions occurred (10.5% vs 2.6%).

pmid:28961722.authors: Best D, Avenell A, Bhattacharya S
pmid:28961722.title: How effective are weight-loss interventions for improving fertility in women and men who are overweight or obese? A systematic review and meta-analysis of the evidence
pmid:28961722.finding: In overweight/obese women, reduced-calorie diet and exercise interventions increased pregnancy (RR 1.59) and improved ovulation; miscarriage was not reduced.

pmid:9688387.authors: Augood C, Duckitt K, Templeton AA
pmid:9688387.title: Smoking and female infertility: a systematic review and meta-analysis
pmid:9688387.finding: Female smokers had higher odds of infertility (OR 1.60) and lower odds of pregnancy per IVF cycle (OR 0.66).

pmid:18927070.authors: Waylen AL, Metwally M, Jones GL, et al.
pmid:18927070.title: Effects of cigarette smoking upon clinical outcomes of assisted reproduction: a meta-analysis
pmid:18927070.finding: Smokers undergoing ART had lower odds of live birth per cycle (OR 0.54) and clinical pregnancy (OR 0.56) and higher miscarriage (OR 2.65).

pmid:30481189.authors: Zhu D, Chung HF, Pandeya N, et al.
pmid:30481189.title: Relationships between intensity, duration, cumulative dose, and timing of smoking with age at menopause: A pooled analysis of individual data from 17 observational studies
pmid:30481189.finding: Current smokers had about twice the risk of premature (RRR 2.05) and early (1.80) menopause, with clear dose-response; women who had quit more than 10 years earlier had the same risk as never smokers.

pmid:18252054.authors: Freour T, Masson D, Mirallie S, et al.
pmid:18252054.title: Active smoking compromises IVF outcome and affects ovarian reserve
pmid:18252054.finding: Active smokers had lower AMH, fewer mature oocytes (8.6 vs 12.1) and lower clinical pregnancy (10% vs 29.6%) than non-smokers.

pmid:38284953.authors: Practice Committee of the American Society for Reproductive Medicine
pmid:38284953.title: Tobacco or marijuana use and infertility: a committee opinion
pmid:38284953.finding: ASRM committee opinion reviewing deleterious effects of tobacco, nicotine and marijuana on conception, ovarian follicular dynamics, gamete mutations and ART outcomes, and smoking-cessation strategies.

pmid:29062133.authors: Fan D, Liu L, Xia Q, et al.
pmid:29062133.title: Female alcohol consumption and fecundability: a systematic review and dose-response meta-analysis
pmid:29062133.finding: Any alcohol use was associated with lower fecundability (RR 0.87); light (<=12.5 g/day) 0.89, moderate-heavy (>12.5 g/day) 0.77; per 12.5 g/day RR 0.98.

pmid:27581754.authors: Mikkelsen EM, Riis AH, Wise LA, et al.
pmid:27581754.title: Alcohol consumption and fecundability: prospective Danish cohort study
pmid:27581754.finding: Fewer than 14 servings/week had no discernible effect on fecundability; >=14 servings/week FR 0.82 (imprecise).

pmid:21173655.authors: Rossi BV, Berry KF, Hornstein MD, et al.
pmid:21173655.title: Effect of alcohol consumption on in vitro fertilization
pmid:21173655.finding: Women drinking >=4 drinks/week had 16% lower odds of IVF live birth (OR 0.84); 21% lower when both partners did.

pmid:28854726.authors: Abadia L, Chiu YH, Williams PL, et al.
pmid:28854726.title: The association between pre-treatment maternal alcohol and caffeine intake and outcomes of assisted reproduction in a prospectively followed cohort
pmid:28854726.finding: Low-to-moderate pre-treatment alcohol (<=12 g/day) and caffeine (<200 mg/day) were not associated with ART outcomes.

pmid:29276412.authors: Lyngsø J, Ramlau-Hansen CH, Bay B, et al.
pmid:29276412.title: Association between coffee or caffeine consumption and fecundity and fertility: a systematic review and dose-response meta-analysis
pmid:29276412.finding: Caffeine was associated with spontaneous abortion (RR 1.37 at 300 mg/day; 2.32 at 600 mg/day) but showed little or no association with fecundability or fertility-treatment outcomes.

pmid:27112524.authors: Wesselink AK, Wise LA, Rothman KJ, et al.
pmid:27112524.title: Caffeine and caffeinated beverage consumption and fecundability in a preconception cohort
pmid:27112524.finding: Female total caffeine intake was not associated with fecundability; male intake >=300 mg/day was (FR 0.72).

pmid:26329421.authors: Chen LW, Wu Y, Neelakantan N, et al.
pmid:26329421.title: Maternal caffeine intake during pregnancy and risk of pregnancy loss: a categorical and dose-response meta-analysis of prospective studies
pmid:26329421.finding: Caffeine in pregnancy: pregnancy-loss RR 1.02 at 50-149 mg/day, 1.16 at 150-349, 1.40 at 350-699, 1.72 at >=700; +7% per 100 mg/day.

pmid:20228391.authors: Legro RS, Sauer MV, Mottla GL, et al.
pmid:20228391.title: Effect of air quality on assisted human reproduction
pmid:20228391.finding: Higher NO2 at home and at the IVF lab was associated with lower live birth (e.g. OR 0.76 per 0.01 ppm after embryo transfer); PM2.5 during culture was associated with lower conception.

pmid:32951044.authors: La Marca A, Spaggiari G, Domenici D, et al.
pmid:32951044.title: Elevated levels of nitrous dioxide are associated with lower AMH levels: a real-world analysis
pmid:32951044.finding: Higher NO2 (and weakly PM10/PM2.5) exposure was associated with lower AMH; NO2 remained associated after age adjustment.

pmid:31241127.authors: Gaskins AJ, Mínguez-Alarcón L, Fong KC, et al.
pmid:31241127.title: Supplemental Folate and the Relationship Between Traffic-Related Air Pollution and Livebirth Among Women Undergoing Assisted Reproduction
pmid:31241127.finding: Among women taking <800 ug/day supplemental folate, each 20 ppb NO2 was associated with 24% lower odds of live birth; no association at >=800 ug/day.

pmid:26545148.authors: Hauser R, Gaskins AJ, Souter I, et al.
pmid:26545148.title: Urinary Phthalate Metabolite Concentrations and Reproductive Outcomes among Women Undergoing in Vitro Fertilization: Results from the EARTH Study
pmid:26545148.finding: Highest vs lowest quartile of urinary DEHP metabolites: fewer oocytes and mature oocytes, and 19 percentage points lower clinical pregnancy and live birth per cycle.

pmid:20002217.authors: Mok-Lin E, Ehrlich S, Williams PL, et al.
pmid:20002217.title: Urinary bisphenol A concentrations and ovarian response among women undergoing IVF
pmid:20002217.finding: Each log-unit increase in urinary BPA was associated with 12% fewer oocytes retrieved and lower peak estradiol.

pmid:34337160.authors: Butts CD, Bloom MS, McGough A, et al.
pmid:34337160.title: Toxic elements in follicular fluid adversely influence the likelihood of pregnancy and live birth in women undergoing IVF
pmid:34337160.finding: Follicular fluid mercury above ~0.51 ug/L and higher lead were associated with lower live birth after IVF (Pb RR 0.68).

pmid:12525451.authors: Wallace WH, Thomson AB, Kelsey TW
pmid:12525451.title: The radiosensitivity of the human oocyte
pmid:12525451.finding: Modelling estimates the radiation dose that destroys half of human oocytes (LD50) at less than 2 Gy.

pmid:29620997.authors: Oktay K, Harvey BE, Partridge AH, et al.
pmid:29620997.title: Fertility Preservation in Patients With Cancer: ASCO Clinical Practice Guideline Update
pmid:29620997.finding: ASCO: discuss infertility risk before cancer treatment as early as possible; oocyte and embryo cryopreservation are standard; GnRH agonists are not a substitute for proven preservation methods.

pmid:19801570.authors: Gudmundsdottir SL, Flanders WD, Augestad LB
pmid:19801570.title: Physical activity and fertility in women: the North-Trøndelag Health Study
pmid:19801570.finding: Women active on most days had 3.2-fold odds of fertility problems and exercising to exhaustion 2.3-fold, vs low activity; no association at lower activity levels.

pmid:27474489.authors: Gaskins AJ, Williams PL, Keller MG, et al.
pmid:27474489.title: Maternal physical and sedentary activities in relation to reproductive outcomes following IVF
pmid:27474489.finding: Pre-treatment moderate-to-vigorous activity (median 2.8 h/week) was not associated with IVF outcomes; some vigorous activities were associated with higher live birth.

pmid:31304974.authors: Mena GP, Mielke GI, Brown WJ
pmid:31304974.title: The effect of physical activity on reproductive health outcomes in young women: a systematic review and meta-analysis
pmid:31304974.finding: Physical-activity interventions increased pregnancy (RR 2.10) and live birth (RR 2.11) vs no therapy in women with reproductive problems (small number of trials).

pmid:30987736.authors: Willis SK, Hatch EE, Wesselink AK, et al.
pmid:30987736.title: Female sleep patterns, shift work, and fecundability in a North American preconception cohort study
pmid:30987736.finding: Trouble sleeping >50% of the time was associated with lower fecundability (FR 0.87); <6 h sleep FR 0.89 (imprecise); shift work was not associated.

pmid:24664130.authors: Lynch CD, Sundaram R, Maisog JM, et al.
pmid:24664130.title: Preconception stress increases the risk of infertility: results from a couple-based prospective cohort study--the LIFE study
pmid:24664130.finding: Highest vs lowest tertile of salivary alpha-amylase (stress marker) was associated with 29% lower fecundability and 2-fold infertility risk; cortisol was not associated.

pmid:21345903.authors: Boivin J, Griffiths E, Venetis CA
pmid:21345903.title: Emotional distress in infertile women and failure of assisted reproductive technologies: meta-analysis of prospective psychosocial studies
pmid:21345903.finding: Pre-treatment anxiety or depression was not associated with pregnancy after a cycle of ART.

pmid:29390148.authors: Karayiannis D, Kontogianni MD, Mendorou C, et al.
pmid:29390148.title: Adherence to the Mediterranean diet and IVF success rate among non-obese women attempting fertility
pmid:29390148.finding: Lowest vs highest tertile of Mediterranean diet score had lower live birth (26.6% vs 48.8%; adjusted RR 0.32); association seen only in women under 35; no effect on oocyte or embryo measures.

pmid:30742825.authors: Gaskins AJ, Nassan FL, Chiu YH, et al.
pmid:30742825.title: Dietary patterns and outcomes of assisted reproduction
pmid:30742825.finding: The profertility diet was associated with 53% higher odds of live birth per SD; top vs bottom quartile +28 percentage points; not related to oocyte counts. Mediterranean diet benefit plateaued after the second quartile.

pmid:20189169.authors: Vujkovic M, de Vries JH, Lindemans J, et al.
pmid:20189169.title: The preconception Mediterranean dietary pattern in couples undergoing in vitro fertilization/intracytoplasmic sperm injection treatment increases the chance of pregnancy
pmid:20189169.finding: High couple adherence to a Mediterranean dietary pattern was associated with higher pregnancy odds after IVF/ICSI (OR 1.4) and higher folate and vitamin B6 in blood and follicular fluid.

pmid:36346903.authors: Muffone ARMC, de Oliveira Lübke PDP, Rabito EI
pmid:36346903.title: Mediterranean diet and infertility: a systematic review with meta-analysis of cohort studies
pmid:36346903.finding: Pooled evidence linking Mediterranean diet adherence to live birth and pregnancy was inconsistent and insufficient to support clinical application.

pmid:28844822.title: Diet and fertility: a review
pmid:28844822.finding: Review: supplemental folic acid (above neural-tube-defect doses) is consistently associated with better fertility; antioxidant supplements do not help women in fertility treatment; omega-3s appear beneficial; vitamin D matters mainly in deficiency.

pmid:17978119.authors: Chavarro JE, Rich-Edwards JW, Rosner BA, et al.
pmid:17978119.title: Diet and lifestyle in the prevention of ovulatory disorder infertility
pmid:17978119.finding: Highest vs lowest quintile of a 'fertility diet' score was associated with 66% lower risk of ovulatory infertility (RR 0.34); five or more low-risk lifestyle factors with 69% lower risk.

pmid:25198264.authors: Gaskins AJ, Afeiche MC, Wright DL, et al.
pmid:25198264.title: Dietary folate and reproductive success among women undergoing assisted reproduction
pmid:25198264.finding: Supplemental folate >800 ug/day vs <400 ug/day was associated with a 20 percentage-point higher live birth rate after ART.

pmid:29149263.authors: Chu J, Gallos I, Tobias A, et al.
pmid:29149263.title: Vitamin D and assisted reproductive treatment outcome: a systematic review and meta-analysis
pmid:29149263.finding: Vitamin D-replete women undergoing ART had higher live birth than deficient/insufficient women (OR 1.33); no association with miscarriage.

pmid:35370977.authors: Zhou X, Wu X, Luo X, et al.
pmid:35370977.title: Effect of Vitamin D Supplementation on In Vitro Fertilization Outcomes: A Trial Sequential Meta-Analysis of 5 Randomized Controlled Trials
pmid:35370977.finding: In vitamin D-deficient infertile women, supplementation raised chemical pregnancy (RR 1.53) but not clinical pregnancy (RR 1.34, NS) or embryo quality.

pmid:29136189.authors: Chiu YH, Karmon AE, Gaskins AJ, et al.
pmid:29136189.title: Serum omega-3 fatty acids and treatment outcomes among women undergoing assisted reproduction
pmid:29136189.finding: Each 1% higher serum long-chain omega-3 was associated with 8% higher probability of live birth after ART.

pmid:22978268.authors: Nehra D, Le HD, Fallon EM, et al.
pmid:22978268.title: Prolonging the female reproductive lifespan and improving egg quality with dietary omega-3 fatty acids
pmid:22978268.finding: In mice, omega-3-rich diets prolonged reproductive function and improved oocyte quality at advanced maternal age; omega-6-rich diets worsened it.

pmid:32851663.authors: Showell MG, Mackenzie-Proctor R, Jordan V, et al.
pmid:32851663.title: Antioxidants for female subfertility
pmid:32851663.finding: Very low-quality evidence: antioxidants might raise live birth (OR 1.81) but evidence is unreliable; 2026 editorial note: 7 included trials since retracted and 2 under expression of concern (conclusions retained).

pmid:29587861.authors: Xu Y, Nisenblat V, Lu C, et al.
pmid:29587861.title: Pretreatment with coenzyme Q10 improves ovarian response and embryo quality in low-prognosis young women with decreased ovarian reserve: a randomized controlled trial
pmid:29587861.n: 186 women <35 with poor ovarian reserve (169 analysed)
pmid:29587861.finding: CoQ10 600 mg/day (200 mg three times daily) for 60 days before IVF increased oocytes retrieved (median 4 vs 2), fertilization and good embryos; live birth 29% vs 16% was not statistically significant.

pmid:26111777.authors: Ben-Meir A, Burstein E, Borrego-Alvarez A, et al.
pmid:26111777.title: Coenzyme Q10 restores oocyte mitochondrial function and fertility during reproductive aging
pmid:26111777.finding: Oocyte ageing in mice and humans involves reduced CoQ-synthesis enzymes and lower ATP; CoQ10 reversed age-related oocyte deficits in mice.

pmid:32767206.authors: Florou P, Anagnostis P, Theocharis P, et al.
pmid:32767206.title: Does coenzyme Q(10) supplementation improve fertility outcomes in women undergoing assisted reproductive technology procedures? A systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized-controlled trials
pmid:32767206.finding: CoQ10 increased clinical pregnancy (28.8% vs 14.1%; OR 2.44) but not live birth (OR 1.67, NS) or miscarriage.

pmid:32045470.authors: Zhang Y, Zhang C, Shu J, et al.
pmid:32045470.title: Adjuvant treatment strategies in ovarian stimulation for poor responders undergoing IVF: a systematic review and network meta-analysis
pmid:32045470.finding: In poor responders, DHEA (OR 2.46) and CoQ10 (OR 2.22) were associated with higher clinical pregnancy vs control; CoQ10 had the lowest cancellation rate.

pmid:32292388.authors: Hu KL, Ye X, Wang S, et al.
pmid:32292388.title: Melatonin Application in Assisted Reproductive Technology: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis of Randomized Trials
pmid:32292388.finding: Melatonin increased clinical pregnancy (OR 1.43) and oocyte/embryo counts but not live birth (OR 1.38, 3 RCTs, NS); low-quality evidence.

pmid:31583699.authors: Fernando S, Wallace EM, Rombauts L, et al.
pmid:31583699.title: The effect of melatonin on ultrasound markers of follicular development: A double-blind placebo-controlled randomised trial
pmid:31583699.journal: Aust N Z J Obstet Gynaecol
pmid:31583699.finding: Melatonin 2, 4 or 8 mg twice daily during IVF stimulation did not change follicle number or ovarian vascular indices vs placebo (pilot).

pmid:30570133.authors: Showell MG, Mackenzie-Proctor R, Jordan V, et al.
pmid:30570133.title: Inositol for subfertile women with polycystic ovary syndrome
pmid:30570133.finding: Very low-quality evidence; uncertain whether myo-inositol improves live birth (OR 2.42, 95% CI 0.75-7.83) or clinical pregnancy in PCOS before IVF.

pmid:38163998.authors: Fitz V, Graca S, Mahalingaiah S, et al.
pmid:38163998.title: Inositol for Polycystic Ovary Syndrome: A Systematic Review and Meta-analysis to Inform the 2023 Update of the International Evidence-based PCOS Guidelines
pmid:38163998.finding: For the 2023 PCOS guideline: inositol evidence is limited and inconclusive; possible metabolic benefits; little difference from metformin for reproductive outcomes.

pmid:26507336.authors: Pacchiarotti A, Carlomagno G, Antonini G, et al.
pmid:26507336.title: Effect of myo-inositol and melatonin versus myo-inositol, in a randomized controlled trial, for improving in vitro fertilization of patients with polycystic ovarian syndrome
pmid:26507336.finding: RETRACTED (2026). Claimed myo-inositol 4 g + folic acid 400 ug + melatonin 3 mg improved oocyte and embryo quality; should not be relied on.

pmid:25653680.authors: Thakker D, Raval A, Patel I, et al.
pmid:25653680.title: N-acetylcysteine for polycystic ovary syndrome: a systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized controlled clinical trials
pmid:25653680.finding: NAC improved ovulation and pregnancy vs placebo but was inferior to metformin; trials had high risk of bias.

pmid:15705376.authors: Rizk AY, Bedaiwy MA, Al-Inany HG
pmid:15705376.title: N-acetyl-cysteine is a novel adjuvant to clomiphene citrate in clomiphene citrate-resistant patients with polycystic ovary syndrome
pmid:15705376.finding: NAC 1.2 g/day added to clomiphene raised ovulation (49.3% vs 1.3%) and pregnancy (21.3% vs 0%) vs placebo.

pmid:38837771.authors: Naik S, Lepine S, Nagels HE, et al.
pmid:38837771.title: Androgens (dehydroepiandrosterone or testosterone) for women undergoing assisted reproduction
pmid:38837771.finding: Cochrane: DHEA probably makes little or no difference to live birth in poor responders (OR 1.30, NS, moderate certainty); testosterone probably improves it (OR 2.53).

pmid:20729538.authors: Wiser A, Gonen O, Ghetler Y, et al.
pmid:20729538.title: Addition of dehydroepiandrosterone (DHEA) for poor-responder patients before and during IVF treatment improves the pregnancy rate: a randomized prospective study
pmid:20729538.finding: DHEA 75 mg/day before and during IVF was associated with higher live birth (23.1% vs 4.0%) in a very small trial.

pmid:25015747.authors: Ismail AM, Hamed AH, Saso S, et al.
pmid:25015747.title: Adding L-carnitine to clomiphene resistant PCOS women improves the quality of ovulation and the pregnancy rate. A randomized clinical trial
pmid:25015747.journal: Eur J Obstet Gynecol Reprod Biol
pmid:25015747.finding: RETRACTED. Claimed L-carnitine 3 g/day with clomiphene raised pregnancy from 5.8% to 51.5%; should not be relied on.

pmid:32273814.title: Preconception resveratrol intake against infertility: Friend or foe?
pmid:32273814.finding: Resveratrol may support ovarian function via SIRT1 but suppresses endometrial decidualization (anti-deciduogenic) and its teratogenicity is unknown; avoid in the luteal phase and pregnancy.

pmid:31160243.authors: Ochiai A, Kuroda K, Ikemoto Y, et al.
pmid:31160243.title: Influence of resveratrol supplementation on IVF-embryo transfer cycle outcomes
pmid:31160243.finding: Resveratrol 200 mg/day during embryo-transfer cycles was associated with lower clinical pregnancy (OR 0.54) and higher miscarriage (OR 2.60).

pmid:38987824.authors: Ardehjani NA, Agha-Hosseini M, Nashtaei MS, et al.
pmid:38987824.title: Resveratrol ameliorates mitochondrial biogenesis and reproductive outcomes in women with polycystic ovary syndrome undergoing assisted reproduction: a randomized, triple-blind, placebo-controlled clinical trial
pmid:38987824.finding: Resveratrol 800 mg/day for 60 days lowered follicular fluid oxidative stress and raised oocyte maturity and good-quality embryos, but pregnancy rates did not differ.

pmid:33345661.authors: Di Tucci C, Galati G, Mattei G, et al.
pmid:33345661.title: The role of alpha lipoic acid in female and male infertility: a systematic review
pmid:33345661.finding: Systematic review (28 articles): alpha-lipoic acid shows some positive effects on oocyte maturation, embryo grade and endometriosis pain, but clinical evidence is limited and more trials are needed.

pmid:32395637.authors: ESHRE Guideline Group on Ovarian Stimulation; Bosch E, Broer S, et al.
pmid:32395637.title: ESHRE guideline: ovarian stimulation for IVF/ICSI(†)
pmid:32395637.finding: ESHRE ovarian stimulation guideline: hormone pre-treatment and adjuvants (metformin, growth hormone, testosterone, DHEA, aspirin, sildenafil) are not recommended for improving efficacy.

pmid:20685716.authors: Dechanet C, Anahory T, Mathieu Daude JC, et al.
pmid:20685716.title: Effects of cigarette smoking on reproduction
pmid:20685716.finding: Systematic review: cigarette smoke contains thousands of toxicants (nicotine, polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons, cadmium) that target folliculogenesis, steroidogenesis and every other reproductive stage, dose-dependently.

pmid:25788567.authors: Hahn KA, Wise LA, Rothman KJ, et al.
pmid:25788567.title: Caffeine and caffeinated beverage consumption and risk of spontaneous abortion
pmid:25788567.finding: Preconception caffeine was not associated with miscarriage (HR 1.09 for >=300 vs <100 mg/day), whereas early-pregnancy intake of 100-299 mg/day was (HR ~1.5-1.6).

pmid:30921477.authors: Lim SS, Hutchison SK, Van Ryswyk E, et al.
pmid:30921477.title: Lifestyle changes in women with polycystic ovary syndrome
pmid:30921477.finding: Cochrane: lifestyle interventions in PCOS may modestly reduce weight and free androgen index; no trial reported live birth or miscarriage.

pmid:32514568.authors: Szymanska KJ, Tan X, Oktay K
pmid:32514568.title: Unraveling the mechanisms of chemotherapy-induced damage to human primordial follicle reserve: road to developing therapeutics for fertility preservation and reversing ovarian aging
pmid:32514568.finding: Gonadotoxic chemotherapy (e.g. cyclophosphamide, doxorubicin) induces DNA double-strand breaks and apoptosis of primordial-follicle oocytes within 12-24 h, plus stromal and microvascular damage.

pmid:30895239.authors: Fernando S, Biggs SN, Horne RSC, et al.
pmid:30895239.title: The impact of melatonin on the sleep patterns of women undergoing IVF: a double blind RCT
pmid:30895239.finding: Melatonin 2, 4 or 8 mg twice daily from cycle day 2 to egg retrieval did not cause daytime sleepiness or change objective sleep vs placebo.

pmid:34517426.authors: Abdelazeem B, Abbas KS, Shehata J, et al.
pmid:34517426.title: The effects of curcumin as dietary supplement for patients with polycystic ovary syndrome: An updated systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized clinical trials.
pmid:34517426.finding: Curcumin improved fasting glucose (-3.7 mg/dL), insulin, HOMA-IR (-0.55) and total cholesterol, with no effect on LDL, HDL, sex hormones, weight or CRP.

pmid:31656219.authors: Azami SH, Nazarian H, Abdollahifar MA, et al.
pmid:31656219.title: The antioxidant curcumin postpones ovarian aging in young and middle-aged mice.
pmid:31656219.finding: In mice, intraperitoneal curcumin (100 mg/kg/day) preserved follicle numbers, AMH and oocyte quality with age.

pmid:22606002.title: Injurious effects of curcumin on maturation of mouse oocytes, fertilization and fetal development via apoptosis.
pmid:22606002.finding: In mice, curcumin (in vitro and 40 uM in drinking water) impaired oocyte maturation, fertilisation and early embryo development via apoptosis.

pmid:33669954.authors: Chien YJ, Chang CY, Wu MY, et al.
pmid:33669954.title: Effects of Curcumin on Glycemic Control and Lipid Profile in Polycystic Ovary Syndrome: Systematic Review with Meta-Analysis and Trial Sequential Analysis.
pmid:33669954.finding: Curcumin improved fasting glucose, insulin, HOMA-IR (-0.32), HDL and total cholesterol but not LDL or triglycerides.

pmid:39461199.authors: Feghhi F, Ghaznavi H, Sheervalilou R, et al.
pmid:39461199.title: Effects of metformin and curcumin in women with polycystic ovary syndrome: A factorial clinical trial.
pmid:39461199.finding: Nanocurcumin 80 mg three times daily plus metformin improved lipids, glucose markers, weight and testosterone more than either agent alone or placebo over 12 weeks.

pmid:36788534.authors: Ghanbarzadeh-Ghashti N, Ghanbari-Homaie S, Shaseb E, et al.
pmid:36788534.title: The effect of Curcumin on metabolic parameters and androgen level in women with polycystic ovary syndrome: a randomized controlled trial.
pmid:36788534.finding: 1000 mg/day curcumin for 12 weeks lowered fasting glucose and reduced amenorrhoea/oligomenorrhoea (13% vs 22%) versus placebo, but did not change lipids, insulin, SHBG, testosterone or hirsutism.

pmid:37818734.authors: Gudarzi R, Shabani F, Mohammad-Alizadeh-Charandabi S, et al.
pmid:37818734.title: Effect of curcumin on painful symptoms of endometriosis: A triple-blind randomized controlled trial.
pmid:37818734.finding: Curcumin 1000 mg/day for 8 weeks did not improve endometriosis pain or quality of life versus placebo.

pmid:40088332.authors: Jannatifar R, Asa E, Cheraghi E, et al.
pmid:40088332.title: Nanomicelle curcumin improves oxidative stress, inflammatory markers, and assisted reproductive techniques outcomes in endometriosis cases: a randomized clinical trial.
pmid:40088332.n: 50 women with stage III/IV endometriosis undergoing ART
pmid:40088332.finding: Nanomicelle curcumin 120 mg/day for 10 weeks improved serum and follicular-fluid oxidative-stress markers and reported more oocytes, mature oocytes and good embryos; small single-centre trial.

pmid:40041784.authors: Mohammadi S, Ziaei S, Morvaridi M, et al.
pmid:40041784.title: Impacts of Curcumin Supplementation on Cardiometabolic Risk Factors in Patients With Polycystic Ovary Syndrome: A Systematic Review and Dose-Response Meta-Analysis.
pmid:40041784.finding: Curcumin modestly lowered fasting glucose, insulin, HOMA-IR (SMD -0.36) and TC, but did not change BMI, testosterone, DHEA, LH or FSH.

pmid:34655047.authors: Simental-Mendía LE, Shah N, Sathyapalan T, et al.
pmid:34655047.title: Effect of Curcumin on Glycaemic and Lipid Parameters in Polycystic Ovary Syndrome: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis of Randomized Controlled Trials.
pmid:34655047.finding: Curcumin lowered fasting glucose (-3.7 mg/dL), insulin and HOMA-IR (-0.94, I2 90%) but did not change any lipid index.

pmid:34939763.authors: Esfandyari S, Aleyasin A, Noroozi Z, et al.
pmid:34939763.title: The Protective Effect of Sulforaphane against Oxidative Stress through Activation of NRF2/ARE Pathway in Human Granulosa Cells.
pmid:34939763.finding: Sulforaphane pretreatment protected human granulosa cells from H2O2-induced ROS and apoptosis via NRF2, SOD and catalase.

pmid:36907095.authors: Feng Z, Wang T, Sun Y, et al.
pmid:36907095.title: Sulforaphane suppresses paraquat-induced oxidative damage in bovine in vitro-matured oocytes through Nrf2 transduction pathway.
pmid:36907095.finding: 1 µM sulforaphane during in vitro maturation raised bovine oocyte maturation and embryo rates and countered paraquat oxidative damage via Nrf2.

pmid:37783421.authors: Li WJ, Zhang X, Shen M, et al.
pmid:37783421.title: Sulforaphane alleviates the meiosis defects induced by 3-nitropropionic acid in mouse oocytes.
pmid:37783421.finding: Sulforaphane alleviated 3-nitropropionic-acid-induced meiotic, spindle and mitochondrial defects in mouse oocytes matured in vitro.

pmid:28583601.authors: Sohel MMH, Konca Y, Akyuz B, et al.
pmid:28583601.title: Concentration dependent antioxidative and apoptotic effects of sulforaphane on bovine granulosa cells in vitro.
pmid:28583601.finding: In bovine granulosa cells, low sulforaphane (2 µM) activated NRF2 antioxidant genes while concentrations above ~15 µM were cytotoxic.

pmid:34678578.authors: Taheri M, Hayati Roudbari N, Amidi F, et al.
pmid:34678578.title: The protective effect of sulforaphane against oxidative stress in granulosa cells of patients with polycystic ovary syndrome (PCOS) through activation of AMPK/AKT/NRF2 signaling pathway.
pmid:34678578.n: granulosa cells from PCOS and control women (in vitro)
pmid:34678578.finding: Sulforaphane reduced ROS and apoptosis in granulosa-lutein cells from women with PCOS, with AMPK/AKT/NRF2 activation.

pmid:37020589.authors: Rostami S, Alyasin A, Saedi M, et al.
pmid:37020589.title: Astaxanthin ameliorates inflammation, oxidative stress, and reproductive outcomes in endometriosis patients undergoing assisted reproduction: A randomized, triple-blind placebo-controlled clinical trial.
pmid:37020589.finding: 6 mg/day astaxanthin for 12 weeks lowered serum MDA and cytokines and increased oocytes, MII oocytes and high-quality embryos.

pmid:39482765.authors: Shafie A, Aleyasin A, Saffari M, et al.
pmid:39482765.title: Astaxanthin improves assisted reproductive technology outcomes in poor ovarian responders through alleviating oxidative stress, inflammation, and apoptosis: a randomized clinical trial.
pmid:39482765.finding: 12 mg/day astaxanthin for 8 weeks increased oocytes retrieved, MII oocytes and high-quality embryos and lowered serum MDA and follicular-fluid IL-6.

pmid:37845508.authors: Zhang Y, Bai J, Cui Z, et al.
