pmid:37845508.title: Polyamine metabolite spermidine rejuvenates oocyte quality by enhancing mitophagy during female reproductive aging.
pmid:37845508.finding: Ovarian spermidine falls with age in mice; supplementation improved follicle development, oocyte maturation and fertility of aged mice by enhancing mitophagy.

pmid:41483483.authors: Arsenaki E, Stathi D, Triantafyllidis KK, et al.
pmid:41483483.title: The effects of ketogenic diet on polycystic ovary syndrome: A systematic review and meta-analysis.
pmid:41483483.finding: In mostly overweight women with PCOS, ketogenic diets reduced weight (-10.8 kg), LH and insulin resistance and shortened cycle length pre-post, and beat other diets for weight and LH; androgen results were inconsistent and heterogeneity high.

pmid:40394635.authors: Cannarella R, Rubulotta M, Leonardi A, et al.
pmid:40394635.title: Effects of ketogenic diets on polycystic ovary syndrome: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
pmid:40394635.finding: High-fat ketogenic and very-low-energy ketogenic diets improved weight, glucose, HOMA, triglycerides and LH in PCOS; two RCTs found no weight advantage over low-calorie diets.

pmid:38565002.authors: de Amorim ALB, Rodrigues EF, Sussi EL, et al.
pmid:38565002.title: Carbohydrate restriction during lactation: A systematic review.
pmid:38565002.finding: Carbohydrate restriction during breastfeeding appears repeatedly in case reports of lactation ketoacidosis requiring hospital care.

pmid:29368448.authors: Desrosiers TA, Siega-Riz AM, Mosley BS, et al.
pmid:29368448.title: Low carbohydrate diets may increase risk of neural tube defects.
pmid:29368448.finding: Women with restricted periconceptional carbohydrate intake (<= 5th percentile) had half the dietary folic acid and 30% higher odds of a neural-tube-defect pregnancy (aOR 1.30, 1.02-1.67).

pmid:36688496.authors: Liu S, Yao Q, Li X, et al.
pmid:36688496.title: Effects of a ketogenic diet on reproductive and metabolic phenotypes in mice with polycystic ovary syndrome†.
pmid:36688496.finding: In DHEA-induced PCOS mice a 3-week ketogenic diet lowered weight and glucose, improved ovarian function in some mice and reduced ovarian inflammation and apoptosis, but impaired glucose tolerance.

pmid:16359551.authors: Mavropoulos JC, Yancy WS, Hepburn J, et al.
pmid:16359551.title: The effects of a low-carbohydrate, ketogenic diet on the polycystic ovary syndrome: a pilot study.
pmid:16359551.finding: A < 20 g/day carbohydrate diet for 24 weeks cut weight 12%, free testosterone 22%, LH/FSH 36% and fasting insulin 54% in PCOS; two women conceived.

pmid:34790167.authors: Shang Y, Zhou H, He R, et al.
pmid:34790167.title: Dietary Modification for Reproductive Health in Women With Polycystic Ovary Syndrome: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
pmid:34790167.finding: Dietary interventions in PCOS increased clinical pregnancy, ovulation and menstrual regularity and lowered miscarriage; low-carbohydrate diets were the best subgroup for reproductive outcomes.

pmid:24168053.authors: Sussman D, Ellegood J, Henkelman M
pmid:24168053.title: A gestational ketogenic diet alters maternal metabolic status as well as offspring physiological growth and brain structure in the neonatal mouse.
pmid:24168053.finding: Gestational ketogenic diet lowered fertility and litter size in mice, put dams at risk of fatal ketoacidosis in lactation, and slowed offspring growth with altered brain structure.

pmid:28110175.authors: van der Louw EJ, Williams TJ, Henry-Barron BJ, et al.
pmid:28110175.title: Ketogenic diet therapy for epilepsy during pregnancy: A case series.
pmid:28110175.finding: Two women with epilepsy stayed on ketogenic/modified Atkins therapy in pregnancy with fewer seizures; one infant had ear deformities of unknown significance; safety not established.

pmid:35856159.authors: Whatley EG, Truong TT, Wilhelm D, et al.
pmid:35856159.title: β-hydroxybutyrate reduces blastocyst viability via trophectoderm-mediated metabolic aberrations in mice.
pmid:35856159.finding: Culturing mouse embryos with BHB at ketogenic-diet levels (2 mmol/L) slowed development, disturbed glycolysis and reduced fetal viability after transfer in a sex-specific way.

pmid:38593828.authors: Whatley EG, Harvey AJ, Gardner DK
pmid:38593828.title: A maternal ketogenic diet alters oviduct fluid nutrients and embryo histone acetylation in mice.
pmid:38593828.finding: A maternal ketogenic diet for 24-27 days raised BHB in mouse blood and oviduct fluid, delayed blastocyst development and reduced trophectoderm histone acetylation.

pmid:40674330.authors: Zala SM, Santos R, Strasser E, et al.
pmid:40674330.title: Sex-dependent effects of a gestational ketogenic diet on offspring birth and lifespan.
pmid:40674330.finding: A ketogenic diet in the second half of mouse pregnancy reduced litter size and the proportion of female pups and shortened male offspring lifespan.

pmid:31885557.authors: Zhang X, Zheng Y, Guo Y, et al.
pmid:31885557.title: The Effect of Low Carbohydrate Diet on Polycystic Ovary Syndrome: A Meta-Analysis of Randomized Controlled Trials.
pmid:31885557.finding: Low-carbohydrate diets (< 45% energy) lowered BMI, HOMA-IR and LDL in PCOS; those lasting > 4 weeks raised SHBG and FSH and lowered testosterone.

pmid:39785103.authors: Al-Taiar A, Rahman ME, Salama M, et al.
pmid:39785103.title: Impacts of Ramadan fasting during pregnancy on pregnancy and birth outcomes: An umbrella review.
pmid:39785103.finding: Umbrella review: insufficient evidence that Ramadan fasting in pregnancy shortens gestation or reduces birth weight, but evidence quality is low and no firm guidance is possible.

pmid:9435419.authors: Alvero R, Kimzey L, Sebring N, et al.
pmid:9435419.title: Effects of fasting on neuroendocrine function and follicle development in lean women.
pmid:9435419.finding: In lean women a 72-h follicular-phase fast cut LH pulses 19%; 2 of 7 fasted cycles were anovulatory and follicular phases lengthened.

pmid:30359228.authors: Glazier JD, Hayes DJL, Hussain S, et al.
pmid:30359228.title: The effect of Ramadan fasting during pregnancy on perinatal outcomes: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
pmid:30359228.finding: Ramadan fasting in pregnancy did not affect birth weight or preterm delivery; lower placental weight came mainly from one large study; no perinatal mortality data.

pmid:33849562.authors: Li C, Xing C, Zhang J, et al.
pmid:33849562.title: Eight-hour time-restricted feeding improves endocrine and metabolic profiles in women with anovulatory polycystic ovary syndrome.
pmid:33849562.finding: 5 weeks of 8-h TRE (single arm) lowered weight, testosterone, free androgen index, insulin and hsCRP, raised SHBG, and improved menstrual regularity in 11 of 15 women.

pmid:12519869.title: Luteinizing hormone pulsatility is disrupted at a threshold of energy availability in regularly menstruating women.
pmid:12519869.finding: LH pulsatility was unaffected at an energy availability of 30 kcal/kg lean mass/day but disrupted below that threshold (10-20 kcal/kg).

pmid:6121184.authors: Metzger BE, Ravnikar V, Vileisis RA, et al.
pmid:6121184.title: "Accelerated starvation" and the skipped breakfast in late normal pregnancy.
pmid:6121184.finding: Extending the overnight fast from 12 to 18 h in late pregnancy ('skipped breakfast') caused falling glucose and rising fatty acids and beta-hydroxybutyrate ('accelerated starvation'); non-pregnant women barely changed.

pmid:7714088.authors: Olson BR, Cartledge T, Sebring N, et al.
pmid:7714088.title: Short-term fasting affects luteinizing hormone secretory dynamics but not reproductive function in normal-weight sedentary women.
pmid:7714088.finding: A 3-day mid-follicular fast reduced LH pulses but did not alter follicle growth, ovulation or cycle length in normal-weight women.

pmid:40806019.authors: Ranneh Y, Hamsho M, Shkorfu W, et al.
pmid:40806019.title: Effect of Intermittent Fasting on Anthropometric Measurements, Metabolic Profile, and Hormones in Women with Polycystic Ovary Syndrome: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
pmid:40806019.finding: In PCOS, IF reduced weight (-4.25 kg), insulin resistance, free androgen index and DHEA-S and raised SHBG; total testosterone and AMH did not change.

pmid:1881416.authors: Rizzo T, Metzger BE, Burns WJ, et al.
pmid:1881416.title: Correlations between antepartum maternal metabolism and intelligence of offspring.
pmid:1881416.finding: Higher third-trimester maternal beta-hydroxybutyrate correlated with lower offspring IQ scores at ages 2-5 (r about -0.2), observational.

pmid:39143654.authors: Talebi S, Shab-Bidar S, Moini A, et al.
pmid:39143654.title: The effects of time-restricted eating alone or in combination with probiotic supplementation in comparison with a calorie-restricted diet on endocrine and metabolic profiles in women with polycystic ovary syndrome: A randomized clinical trial.
pmid:39143654.finding: 8 weeks of 14:10 early TRE (with or without probiotics) gave no greater weight loss or menstrual, androgen or metabolic improvement than daily calorie restriction.

pmid:33945905.authors: Björvang RD, Hassan J, Stefopoulou M, et al.
pmid:33945905.title: Persistent organic pollutants and the size of ovarian reserve in reproductive-aged women.
pmid:33945905.finding: PFAS were not associated with AMH or follicle density, whereas some organochlorines (HCB, PCBs) were linked to fewer non-growing follicles.

pmid:36801327.authors: Cohen NJ, Yao M, Midya V, et al.
pmid:36801327.title: Exposure to perfluoroalkyl substances and women's fertility outcomes in a Singaporean population-based preconception cohort.
pmid:36801327.finding: Each quartile increase in individual PFAS (PFDA, PFOS) was associated with 5-10% lower fecundability and lower odds of clinical pregnancy.

pmid:19176540.authors: Fei C, McLaughlin JK, Lipworth L, et al.
pmid:19176540.title: Maternal levels of perfluorinated chemicals and subfecundity.
pmid:19176540.finding: Higher plasma PFOS and PFOA were associated with longer time to pregnancy (fecundity odds ratios ~0.6-0.75 in upper quartiles).

pmid:22317809.authors: Fei C, Weinberg CR, Olsen J
pmid:22317809.title: Commentary: perfluorinated chemicals and time to pregnancy: a link based on reverse causation?
pmid:22317809.finding: Commentary by Fei, Weinberg and Olsen asking whether PFAS-time-to-pregnancy links reflect reverse causation (longer gaps since last pregnancy/breastfeeding let PFAS build up).

pmid:35636536.authors: Hong A, Zhuang L, Cui W, et al.
pmid:35636536.title: Per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFAS) exposure in women seeking in vitro fertilization-embryo transfer treatment (IVF-ET) in China: Blood-follicular transfer and associations with IVF-ET outcomes.
pmid:35636536.finding: PFAS crossed readily from blood into follicular fluid (transfer 0.65-0.92) but showed no clear association with IVF outcomes.

pmid:30731307.authors: Wang W, Zhou W, Wu S, et al.
pmid:30731307.title: Perfluoroalkyl substances exposure and risk of polycystic ovarian syndrome related infertility in Chinese women.
pmid:30731307.finding: Most PFAS did not differ between PCOS-related infertility cases and controls; only PFDoA was associated with higher odds (OR 3.0 top vs bottom tertile).

pmid:22081060.authors: Whitworth KW, Haug LS, Baird DD, et al.
pmid:22081060.title: Perfluorinated compounds and subfecundity in pregnant women.
pmid:22081060.finding: Higher PFOS/PFOA was linked to subfecundity only in parous women (OR ~2.1), not in nulliparous women (OR 0.5-0.7), pointing to reverse causation.

pmid:40334213.authors: Xu J, Wang Q, Jiao X, et al.
pmid:40334213.title: Association between Perfluorooctanoic Acid-Related Poor Embryo Quality and Metabolite Alterations in Human Follicular Fluid during IVF: A Cohort Study.
pmid:40334213.finding: A follicular-fluid PFAS mixture, driven by PFOA, was associated with a lower high-quality embryo rate and lower clinical pregnancy.

pmid:37134253.authors: Zhan W, Qiu W, Ao Y, et al.
pmid:37134253.title: Environmental Exposure to Emerging Alternatives of Per- and Polyfluoroalkyl Substances and Polycystic Ovarian Syndrome in Women Diagnosed with Infertility: A Mixture Analysis.
pmid:37134253.finding: A PFAS mixture, led by emerging alternatives (6:2 Cl-PFESA, HFPO-DA), was associated with higher odds of PCOS (OR 1.20 per ln-unit).

pmid:37486661.title: Treatment and Management of Mental Health Conditions During Pregnancy and Postpartum: ACOG Clinical Practice Guideline No. 5.
pmid:37486661.finding: ACOG Clinical Practice Guideline No. 5 on treating perinatal depression and anxiety, supporting SSRIs as first-line pharmacotherapy and individualized decisions rather than stopping effective treatment.

pmid:26827878.authors: Casilla-Lennon MM, Meltzer-Brody S, Steiner AZ
pmid:26827878.title: The effect of antidepressants on fertility.
pmid:26827878.finding: Cycle-specific antidepressant use was associated with lower fecundability (FR 0.75, CI crossing 1; 0.66 after adjusting for depression history), with confounding by depression unresolved.

pmid:38079178.authors: Cesta CE, Rotem R, Bateman BT, et al.
pmid:38079178.title: Safety of GLP-1 Receptor Agonists and Other Second-Line Antidiabetics in Early Pregnancy.
pmid:38079178.n: 51,826 infants of mothers with type 2 diabetes (Nordic, US, Israel)
pmid:38079178.finding: First-trimester GLP-1 agonist exposure was not associated with more major congenital malformations than insulin (adjusted RR 0.95, 0.72-1.26).

pmid:41860479.title: The effects of glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists on fertility, contraception, and pregnancy: clinical perspectives.
pmid:41860479.journal: Eur J Contracept Reprod Health Care
pmid:41860479.finding: GLP-1 agonists help obesity-related infertility (notably PCOS); clinicians should counsel on contraceptive reliability, ensure washout before conception and note limited pregnancy-safety data.

pmid:39181497.authors: Drummond RF, Seif KE, Reece EA
pmid:39181497.title: Glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonist use in pregnancy: a review.
pmid:39181497.finding: AJOG review: malformation data lack glycemic-control information, so periconceptional safety cannot be concluded; recommends contraception for all patients on GLP-1 agonists.

egg:med-fda-wegovy2021.authors: US Food and Drug Administration; Novo Nordisk
egg:med-fda-wegovy2021.title: WEGOVY (semaglutide) injection, prescribing information (revised 06/2021)
egg:med-fda-wegovy2021.finding: Label section 8.3: discontinue semaglutide at least 2 months before a planned pregnancy because of its long half-life; discontinue when pregnancy is recognized.

egg:med-fda-zepbound2023.authors: US Food and Drug Administration; Eli Lilly
egg:med-fda-zepbound2023.title: ZEPBOUND (tirzepatide) injection, prescribing information (revised 11/2023)
egg:med-fda-zepbound2023.finding: A single 5 mg tirzepatide dose cut ethinyl estradiol Cmax 59% and AUC 20%; users of oral contraceptives should switch to a non-oral method or add a barrier method for 4 weeks after starting and after each dose escalation.

pmid:41701618.authors: Forslund M, Wändell P, Forsberg L, et al.
pmid:41701618.title: GLP-1 receptor agonist treatment in women with polycystic ovary syndrome-a systematic review and meta-analysis.
pmid:41701618.finding: Meta-analysis informing the PCOS guideline: GLP-1 agonists as add-on lowered BMI by 1.38 kg/m2 (low certainty); evidence on reproductive, metabolic and psychological outcomes remains insufficient.

pmid:30062044.title: Return of fertility after discontinuation of contraception: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
pmid:30062044.finding: 83.1% of women conceived within 12 months of stopping contraception, with no difference between hormonal methods and IUDs or by duration of pill use.

pmid:31229399.authors: Han Y, Li Y, He B
pmid:31229399.title: GLP-1 receptor agonists versus metformin in PCOS: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
pmid:31229399.finding: Versus metformin, GLP-1 agonists improved insulin sensitivity and lowered BMI and waist more in PCOS, with more nausea; evidence moderate to low.

pmid:41852577.authors: Hviid KVR, Banasik K, Mortensen LH, et al.
pmid:41852577.title: Periconceptional GLP-1 receptor agonist exposure and obstetric outcomes: a Danish nationwide cohort study.
pmid:41852577.finding: Periconceptional liraglutide or semaglutide was linked to preterm birth only in women with diabetes (aOR ~1.7-1.8), not in those using them for weight management, pointing to the underlying diabetes.

pmid:27131586.authors: Nillni YI, Wesselink AK, Gradus JL, et al.
pmid:27131586.title: Depression, anxiety, and psychotropic medication use and fecundability.
pmid:27131586.finding: Severe depressive symptoms lowered fecundability (FR 0.62) regardless of treatment; psychotropic medication use itself did not appear to harm fecundability.

pmid:41885132.authors: Ozbek L, Shah E, Al-Shiab R, et al.
pmid:41885132.title: Safety of GLP-1 and Dual GLP-1/GIP Receptor Agonists in Preconception, Pregnancy, and Lactation: A Systematic Review of Maternal, Fetal, and Neonatal Outcomes.
pmid:41885132.finding: Periconceptional or early-pregnancy GLP-1-based therapy was not consistently linked to malformations, growth restriction, stillbirth or neonatal death; data on continued use through pregnancy are limited.

pmid:29703793.authors: Salamun V, Jensterle M, Janez A, et al.
pmid:29703793.title: Liraglutide increases IVF pregnancy rates in obese PCOS women with poor response to first-line reproductive treatments: a pilot randomized study.
pmid:29703793.finding: Pilot open-label trial: 12 weeks of liraglutide 1.2 mg plus metformin before IVF (with a 4-week washout) gave higher pregnancy rate per transfer (85.7% vs 28.6%) than metformin alone despite similar weight loss.

pmid:37940101.authors: Skelley JW, Swearengin K, York AL, et al.
pmid:37940101.title: The impact of tirzepatide and glucagon-like peptide 1 receptor agonists on oral hormonal contraception.
pmid:37940101.finding: Tirzepatide significantly reduced oral-contraceptive exposure (AUC, Cmax) via delayed gastric emptying, whereas studies of other GLP-1 agonists showed no clinically significant effect.

pmid:8646437.authors: Smith G, Roberts R, Hall C, et al.
pmid:8646437.title: Reversible ovulatory failure associated with the development of luteinized unruptured follicles in women with inflammatory arthritis taking non-steroidal anti-inflammatory drugs.
pmid:8646437.finding: Three women with inflammatory arthritis had recurrent luteinized unruptured follicles on NSAIDs, with normal ovulation after stopping.

pmid:33177047.authors: Yland JJ, Bresnick KA, Hatch EE, et al.
pmid:33177047.title: Pregravid contraceptive use and fecundability: prospective cohort study.
pmid:33177047.finding: Return to normal fertility took about 5-8 cycles after injectables (FR 0.65), 4 after the patch, 3 after pill or ring and 2 after IUDs or implants; total years of hormonal use did not matter.

pmid:38908019.title: The role of endometrial scratching in IVF/ICSI: a critical appraisal of individual participant data meta-analysis
pmid:38908019.finding: Critical letter questioning the methods and conclusions of the endometrial scratching IPD meta-analysis (with author reply).

pmid:31140578.authors: Armstrong S, Bhide P, Jordan V, et al.
pmid:31140578.title: Time-lapse systems for embryo incubation and assessment in assisted reproduction
pmid:31140578.finding: Cochrane: low to very low quality evidence; no clear difference in live birth/ongoing pregnancy with time-lapse systems (OR 0.91, 95% CI 0.67-1.23).

pmid:33280722.authors: Practice Committee of the American Society for Reproductive Medicine
pmid:33280722.title: Testing and interpreting measures of ovarian reserve: a committee opinion
pmid:33280722.finding: ASRM: ovarian reserve markers (AMH, AFC, FSH) predict egg yield after stimulation but are poor predictors of reproductive potential independent of age.

pmid:34148587.authors: Practice Committee of the American Society for Reproductive Medicine
pmid:34148587.title: Evidence-based outcomes after oocyte cryopreservation for donor oocyte in vitro fertilization and planned oocyte cryopreservation: a guideline
pmid:34148587.finding: ASRM guideline: insufficient evidence to predict live birth after planned egg freezing; outcomes appear better when frozen younger; neonatal outcomes similar to fresh eggs.

pmid:38430080.authors: Ethics Committee of the American Society for Reproductive Medicine
pmid:38430080.title: Planned oocyte cryopreservation to preserve future reproductive potential: an Ethics Committee opinion
pmid:38430080.finding: ASRM Ethics Committee: planned egg freezing is ethically permissible; people must be told about uncertain efficacy and long-term effects.

pmid:38423539.authors: Barrenetxea G, Celis R, Barrenetxea J, et al.
pmid:38423539.title: Intraovarian platelet-rich plasma injection and IVF outcomes in patients with poor ovarian response: a double-blind randomized controlled trial
pmid:38423539.finding: Double-blind RCT: intraovarian PRP slightly raised cumulative mature eggs (10.45 vs 8.91) over three retrievals but not euploid blastocysts (0.81 vs 0.81).

pmid:39033010.authors: Bhide P, Chan DYL, Lanz D, et al.
pmid:39033010.title: Clinical effectiveness and safety of time-lapse imaging systems for embryo incubation and selection in in-vitro fertilisation treatment (TILT): a multicentre, three-parallel-group, double-blind, randomised controlled trial
pmid:39033010.finding: TILT trial: live birth 33.7% with time-lapse imaging, 36.6% with undisturbed culture and 33.0% with standard care (aOR 1.04 and 1.20, both non-significant).

pmid:33712289.authors: Blakemore JK, Grifo JA, DeVore SM, et al.
pmid:33712289.title: Planned oocyte cryopreservation-10-15-year follow-up: return rates and cycle outcomes
pmid:33712289.finding: 10-15-year follow-up of planned egg freezing (mean age 38.2): 38.1% returned; live birth 33.8% among those with outcomes; 58.9% non-use.

pmid:35771604.authors: Boomsma CM, Kamath MS, Keay SD, et al.
pmid:35771604.title: Peri-implantation glucocorticoid administration for assisted reproductive technology cycles
pmid:35771604.finding: Cochrane: uncertain whether peri-implantation glucocorticoids improve live birth (OR 1.37, 95% CI 0.69-2.71; very low certainty).

pmid:20667894.authors: Broer SL, Dólleman M, Opmeer BC, et al.
pmid:20667894.title: AMH and AFC as predictors of excessive response in controlled ovarian hyperstimulation: a meta-analysis
pmid:20667894.finding: AMH and AFC both predict excessive ovarian response (sensitivity ~82%, specificity 76-80%).

pmid:23188168.authors: Broer SL, van Disseldorp J, Broeze KA, et al.
pmid:23188168.title: Added value of ovarian reserve testing on patient characteristics in the prediction of ovarian response and ongoing pregnancy: an individual patient data approach
pmid:23188168.finding: AMH and AFC predict poor ovarian response well (AUC 0.78 and 0.76) but add nothing to age for predicting ongoing pregnancy after IVF.

pmid:21130690.title: Oxidative stress
pmid:21130690.journal: Best Pract Res Clin Obstet Gynaecol
pmid:21130690.finding: Review of reactive oxygen species in the placenta: physiological signalling at low levels, and involvement in miscarriage, pre-eclampsia and membrane rupture at high levels.

pmid:31307997.authors: Burton GJ, Redman CW, Roberts JM, et al.
pmid:31307997.title: Pre-eclampsia: pathophysiology and clinical implications
pmid:31307997.finding: BMJ review: pre-eclampsia arises from syncytiotrophoblast stress; early-onset from defective placentation, late-onset from placental senescence plus maternal cardiometabolic predisposition.

pmid:34798051.authors: Capalbo A, Poli M, Rienzi L, et al.
pmid:34798051.title: Mosaic human preimplantation embryos and their developmental potential in a prospective, non-selection clinical trial
pmid:34798051.finding: Non-selection trial (Igenomix authors): low- and medium-grade mosaic embryos had live birth and miscarriage rates equivalent to euploid embryos, implying PGT-A labels can discard viable embryos.

pmid:26688429.authors: Cobo A, García-Velasco JA, Coello A, et al.
pmid:26688429.title: Oocyte vitrification as an efficient option for elective fertility preservation
pmid:26688429.finding: Elective egg freezing: cumulative live birth with 10-15 vitrified eggs reached ~85% at <=35 years vs ~36% plateau at >=36; 8-10 mature eggs needed for reasonable success; 9.3% had returned.

pmid:27031375.title: Why all women should freeze their eggs
pmid:27031375.finding: IVI review arguing for elective egg freezing: success is best when frozen before 35, but studies show freezing is most cost-effective at 37-38.

pmid:21529757.authors: Conde-Agudelo A, Romero R, Kusanovic JP, et al.
pmid:21529757.title: Supplementation with vitamins C and E during pregnancy for the prevention of preeclampsia and other adverse maternal and perinatal outcomes: a systematic review and metaanalysis
pmid:21529757.finding: Vitamins C and E did not prevent pre-eclampsia (9.6% vs 9.6%) and increased gestational hypertension and premature rupture of membranes.

pmid:32898291.authors: Cornelisse S, Zagers M, Kostova E, et al.
pmid:32898291.title: Preimplantation genetic testing for aneuploidies (abnormal number of chromosomes) in in vitro fertilisation
pmid:32898291.finding: Cochrane: uncertain whether PGT-A increases cumulative live birth; low to moderate quality evidence; possible reduction in miscarriage.

pmid:30341915.authors: Craciunas L, Tsampras N, Raine-Fenning N, et al.
pmid:30341915.title: Intrauterine administration of human chorionic gonadotropin (hCG) for subfertile women undergoing assisted reproduction
pmid:30341915.finding: Cochrane: intrauterine hCG >=500 IU improved live birth only with cleavage-stage transfer (moderate quality); insufficient evidence for blastocyst transfer; no reduction in miscarriage.

pmid:26372034.authors: Depmann M, Broer SL, van der Schouw YT, et al.
pmid:26372034.title: Can we predict age at natural menopause using ovarian reserve tests or mother's age at menopause? A systematic literature review
pmid:26372034.finding: AMH is the most promising predictor of age at natural menopause but prediction intervals are too wide for individual use.

pmid:26604065.authors: Doyle JO, Richter KS, Lim J, et al.
pmid:26604065.title: Successful elective and medically indicated oocyte vitrification and warming for autologous in vitro fertilization, with predicted birth probabilities for fertility preservation according to number of cryopreserved oocytes and age at retrieval
pmid:26604065.finding: Vitrified eggs performed as well as fresh; overall vitrified egg-to-baby efficiency was 6.4% per egg, falling with age at retrieval.

pmid:36472596.authors: Doyle N, Jahandideh S, Hill MJ, et al.
pmid:36472596.title: Effect of Timing by Endometrial Receptivity Testing vs Standard Timing of Frozen Embryo Transfer on Live Birth in Patients Undergoing In Vitro Fertilization: A Randomized Clinical Trial
pmid:36472596.finding: Euploid frozen transfers timed by endometrial receptivity testing did not improve live birth (58.5% vs 61.9%; RR 0.95, 95% CI 0.79-1.13).

pmid:31684684.authors: Duley L, Meher S, Hunter KE, et al.
pmid:31684684.title: Antiplatelet agents for preventing pre-eclampsia and its complications
pmid:31684684.finding: Cochrane: antiplatelet agents cut proteinuric pre-eclampsia by 18% (RR 0.82; NNT 61), preterm birth by 9% and fetal/neonatal death by 14%; may slightly increase postpartum haemorrhage.

pmid:33225079.authors: ESHRE Guideline Group on Female Fertility Preservation
pmid:33225079.title: ESHRE guideline: female fertility preservation
pmid:33225079.finding: ESHRE female fertility preservation guideline covering medical and age-related egg freezing; 78 recommendations, mostly low or very low quality evidence.

pmid:37332387.authors: ESHRE Working Group on Recurrent Implantation Failure; Cimadomo D, de Los Santos MJ, Griesinger G, et al.
pmid:37332387.title: ESHRE good practice recommendations on recurrent implantation failure
pmid:37332387.finding: ESHRE recurrent implantation failure recommendations: RIF defined by a >60% predicted cumulative implantation chance; investigations and interventions graded recommended, to consider, or not recommended.

pmid:31965189.authors: Finkelstein JS, Lee H, Karlamangla A, et al.
pmid:31965189.title: Antimullerian Hormone and Impending Menopause in Late Reproductive Age: The Study of Women's Health Across the Nation
pmid:31965189.n: SWAN women in late reproductive age
pmid:31965189.finding: In women in their late 40s, very low AMH (<10 pg/mL) predicted the final period within 12 months (51-79% by age); AMH outperformed FSH.

pmid:32299733.authors: Gardner DK, Kuramoto T, Tanaka M, et al.
pmid:32299733.title: Prospective randomized multicentre comparison on sibling oocytes comparing G-Series media system with antioxidants versus standard G-Series media system
pmid:32299733.finding: Antioxidants (acetyl-L-carnitine, NAC, alpha-lipoic acid) in culture media raised good day-3 embryos (50.2% vs 40.7%) and, in women 35-40, ongoing pregnancy (50% vs 25.8%); no live-birth primary outcome.

pmid:28166330.authors: Goldman RH, Racowsky C, Farland LV, et al.
pmid:28166330.title: Predicting the likelihood of live birth for elective oocyte cryopreservation: a counseling tool for physicians and patients
pmid:28166330.finding: Counselling model predicting chance of 1-3 live births from age at retrieval and number of mature eggs frozen; derived from fresh ICSI data, not returning egg-freezers.

pmid:19076941.title: In favour of freezing eggs for non-medical reasons
pmid:19076941.finding: Bioethics argument in favour of egg freezing for non-medical reasons (autonomy, equality in work, time to find a partner).

pmid:27890864.authors: Heneghan C, Spencer EA, Bobrovitz N, et al.
pmid:27890864.title: Lack of evidence for interventions offered in UK fertility centres
pmid:27890864.finding: Oxford CEBM analysis: most interventions offered on UK fertility centre websites lacked supporting high-quality evidence.

pmid:38725194.authors: Herlihy NS, Cakiroglu Y, Whitehead C, et al.
pmid:38725194.title: Effect of intraovarian platelet-rich plasma injection on IVF outcomes in women with poor ovarian response: the PROVA randomized controlled trial
pmid:38725194.finding: PROVA trial: intraovarian PRP did not change mature eggs (2.8 vs 3.1), euploid blastocysts, AMH, AFC or sustained implantation.

pmid:32876946.authors: Heymann D, Vidal L, Or Y, et al.
pmid:32876946.title: Hyaluronic acid in embryo transfer media for assisted reproductive technologies
pmid:32876946.finding: Cochrane: functional hyaluronan (0.5 mg/mL) in transfer medium probably raises live birth (RR 1.21, 95% CI 1.10-1.31; moderate certainty; ~33% -> 37-44%) but also raises multiple pregnancy (RR 1.45).

pmid:35595183.authors: Heymann D, Vidal L, Shoham Z, et al.
pmid:35595183.title: The effect of hyaluronic acid in embryo transfer media in donor oocyte cycles and autologous oocyte cycles: a systematic review and meta-analysis
pmid:35595183.finding: Hyaluronan transfer medium raised live birth from 32% to 39% with women's own eggs (RR 1.22; NNT 14), with more multiple pregnancies (NNH 13); little effect in donor-egg cycles.

egg:fer-hfea2026.title: Treatment add-ons with limited evidence (HFEA add-ons rating list)
egg:fer-hfea2026.finding: HFEA traffic-light ratings for 'chances of having a baby' (page reviewed 28 Sep 2026; ratings set by SCAAC): yellow/amber (unclear) for endometrial scratching, hyaluronate-enriched transfer medium and elective freeze-all; grey (insufficient evidence) for assisted hatching, androgens, intralipids, IMSI, intrauterine culture, microbiome testing and SDF-guided treatments; black (no effect) for time-lapse imaging and PICSI; red (no benefit and/or safety concerns) for endometrial receptivity testing, IVIG, steroids, PRP and PGT-A (PGT-A rated green for reducing miscarriage). No green rating for live birth.

egg:fer-hfea2026prp.title: Platelet-rich plasma (PRP): treatment add-on rating
egg:fer-hfea2026prp.finding: Intraovarian PRP for poor/diminished ovarian reserve and intrauterine PRP for thin endometrium, recurrent implantation failure, Asherman's syndrome and recurrent pregnancy loss all rated red (safety concerns, no moderate/high-quality evidence); not rated for most patients because there is no medical reason to offer it. Reviewed 27 Feb 2026.

pmid:42789480.authors: Iwarsson E, Bergh C, Lundin K, et al.
pmid:42789480.title: PGT-A, the theory versus the evidence: a systematic review on efficacy, safety, and cost-effectiveness
pmid:42789480.finding: Systematic review (Swedish HTA-style): live birth per randomised woman was similar with and without PGT-A, both first transfer (OR 1.16, 0.94-1.45) and cumulative (OR 0.87, 0.64-1.19), including over 35; no shorter time to live birth; PGT-A nearly doubles IVF cost.

pmid:37004670.authors: Kieslinger DC, Vergouw CG, Ramos L, et al.
pmid:37004670.title: Clinical outcomes of uninterrupted embryo culture with or without time-lapse-based embryo selection versus interrupted standard culture (SelecTIMO): a three-armed, multicentre, double-blind, randomised controlled trial
pmid:37004670.finding: SelecTIMO: 12-month cumulative ongoing pregnancy 50.8% (time-lapse selection), 50.9% (time-lapse culture) and 49.4% (standard), p=0.85.

pmid:30477915.authors: Labarta E, de Los Santos MJ, Herraiz S, et al.
pmid:30477915.title: Autologous mitochondrial transfer as a complementary technique to intracytoplasmic sperm injection to improve embryo quality in patients undergoing in vitro fertilization-a randomized pilot study
pmid:30477915.finding: AUGMENT pilot RCT (stopped): autologous mitochondrial transfer gave fewer blastocysts (23.3% vs 41.1%) and equal live birth per transferred embryo (41.6% vs 41.2%).

pmid:33730422.authors: Lacey L, Hassan S, Franik S, et al.
pmid:33730422.title: Assisted hatching on assisted conception (in vitro fertilisation (IVF) and intracytoplasmic sperm injection (ICSI))
pmid:33730422.finding: Cochrane: uncertain whether assisted hatching improves live birth (OR 1.09, 95% CI 0.92-1.29; low quality); may slightly increase multiple pregnancy (OR 1.38).

pmid:30673547.authors: Lensen S, Osavlyuk D, Armstrong S, et al.
pmid:30673547.title: A Randomized Trial of Endometrial Scratching before In Vitro Fertilization
pmid:30673547.finding: PIP trial: endometrial scratching before IVF gave identical live birth to no intervention (26.1% vs 26.1%; aOR 1.00, 95% CI 0.78-1.27), with median pain 3.5/10.

pmid:33942073.authors: Lensen S, Hammarberg K, Polyakov A, et al.
pmid:33942073.title: How common is add-on use and how do patients decide whether to use them? A national survey of IVF patients
pmid:33942073.finding: In an Australian national survey, 82% of IVF patients had used at least one add-on, usually at extra cost; half assumed add-ons were known to be safe and 66% reported some regret.

pmid:24238107.authors: Li J, Chen Y, Liu C, et al.
pmid:24238107.title: Intravenous immunoglobulin treatment for repeated IVF/ICSI failure and unexplained infertility: a systematic review and a meta-analysis
pmid:24238107.finding: Meta-analysis mixing randomised and case-control studies reported higher live birth with IVIG after repeated IVF failure (RR 1.62); low-quality evidence.

pmid:20580423.authors: McCance DR, Holmes VA, Maresh MJ, et al.
pmid:20580423.title: Vitamins C and E for prevention of pre-eclampsia in women with type 1 diabetes (DAPIT): a randomised placebo-controlled trial
pmid:20580423.finding: DAPIT: vitamins C and E did not significantly reduce pre-eclampsia (15% vs 19%; RR 0.81, 0.59-1.12); authors suggested testing women with low antioxidant status.

pmid:36809321.authors: Mendoza M, Bonacina E, Garcia-Manau P, et al.
pmid:36809321.title: Aspirin Discontinuation at 24 to 28 Weeks' Gestation in Pregnancies at High Risk of Preterm Preeclampsia: A Randomized Clinical Trial
pmid:36809321.finding: StopPRE: stopping aspirin at 24-28 weeks in high-risk women with a normal sFlt-1:PlGF ratio was non-inferior to continuing (preterm pre-eclampsia 1.48% vs 1.73%).

pmid:26003658.title: Does company-sponsored egg freezing promote or confine women's reproductive autonomy?
pmid:26003658.finding: Ethical analysis: employer-paid egg freezing is only liberating if women understand limits, feel no pressure and other family-friendly policies are kept; these conditions may be impossible to meet.

pmid:31551155.authors: Munné S, Kaplan B, Frattarelli JL, et al.
pmid:31551155.title: Preimplantation genetic testing for aneuploidy versus morphology as selection criteria for single frozen-thawed embryo transfer in good-prognosis patients: a multicenter randomized clinical trial
pmid:31551155.finding: STAR trial: PGT-A did not improve ongoing pregnancy per intention to treat (41.8% vs 43.5%); a post hoc gain per transfer in women 35-40 was not significant per intention to treat.

pmid:30954433.authors: Norman RJ, Alvino H, Hull LM, et al.
pmid:30954433.title: Human growth hormone for poor responders: a randomized placebo-controlled trial provides no evidence for improved live birth rate
pmid:30954433.finding: LIGHT trial (stopped early): growth hormone in previous poor responders gave 14.5% vs 13.7% live birth (OR 1.07, 0.37-3.10).

pmid:31843071.title: Outcome of in vitro fertilization cycles with preimplantation genetic testing for aneuploidies: let's be honest with one another
pmid:31843071.finding: Editorial arguing that PGT-A results should be reported per started cycle, because per-transfer success rates hide embryos lost to testing.

pmid:42138348.authors: Perera AK, Gan J, Afroz A, et al.
pmid:42138348.title: Endometrial injury in women undergoing in vitro fertilisation (IVF)
pmid:42138348.finding: Cochrane 2026: in low-risk-of-bias trials, the effect of endometrial injury on live birth is unclear (OR 1.12, 95% CI 0.98-1.28; moderate certainty), roughly 27% -> 27-32%; causes mild to moderate pain; conclusion unchanged from 2021.

pmid:16616557.authors: Poston L, Briley AL, Seed PT, et al.
pmid:16616557.title: Vitamin C and vitamin E in pregnant women at risk for pre-eclampsia (VIP trial): randomised placebo-controlled trial
pmid:16616557.finding: VIP trial: vitamin C 1000 mg + vitamin E 400 IU daily did not prevent pre-eclampsia (15% vs 16%) and increased low birthweight (28% vs 24%; RR 1.15).

pmid:20375405.authors: Roberts JM, Myatt L, Spong CY, et al.
pmid:20375405.title: Vitamins C and E to prevent complications of pregnancy-associated hypertension
pmid:20375405.finding: NICHD MFMU trial: vitamins C and E from 9-16 weeks did not reduce pregnancy-associated hypertension complications (6.1% vs 5.7%) or pre-eclampsia (7.2% vs 6.7%).

pmid:28657417.authors: Rolnik DL, Wright D, Poon LC, et al.
pmid:28657417.title: Aspirin versus Placebo in Pregnancies at High Risk for Preterm Preeclampsia
pmid:28657417.finding: ASPRE: aspirin 150 mg nightly from 11-14 to 36 weeks cut preterm pre-eclampsia from 4.3% to 1.6% (OR 0.38) in screen-positive women.

pmid:28433371.authors: Rubio C, Bellver J, Rodrigo L, et al.
pmid:28433371.title: In vitro fertilization with preimplantation genetic diagnosis for aneuploidies in advanced maternal age: a randomized, controlled study
pmid:28433371.n: 205 women of advanced maternal age (326 recruited)
pmid:28433371.finding: In women of advanced maternal age, PGT-A raised delivery per first transfer (52.9% vs 24.2%) and cut miscarriage (2.7% vs 39.0%) and time to pregnancy, but cumulative delivery per patient did not differ.

pmid:26343254.authors: Rumbold A, Ota E, Hori H, et al.
pmid:26343254.title: Vitamin E supplementation in pregnancy
pmid:26343254.finding: Cochrane: vitamin E (with C) did not reduce pre-eclampsia (RR 0.91) or stillbirth, lowered abruption (RR 0.64) but raised term prelabour rupture of membranes (RR 1.77).

pmid:32723696.authors: Simón C, Gómez C, Cabanillas S, et al.
pmid:32723696.title: A 5-year multicentre randomized controlled trial comparing personalized, frozen and fresh blastocyst transfer in IVF
pmid:32723696.finding: Igenomix-led trial of ERA-guided personalised transfer: intention-to-treat outcomes were comparable; per-protocol cumulative live birth was higher (71.2% vs 55.4%), but about 50% of patients dropped out.

pmid:31228675.authors: Singh N, Davis AA, Kumar S, et al.
pmid:31228675.title: The effect of administration of intravenous intralipid on pregnancy outcomes in women with implantation failure after IVF/ICSI with non-donor oocytes: A randomised controlled trial
pmid:31228675.journal: Eur J Obstet Gynecol Reprod Biol
pmid:31228675.finding: Small RCT: intravenous intralipid after implantation failure raised live birth (28.8% vs 10%).

pmid:34808697.authors: Sood A, Mohiyiddeen G, Ahmad G, et al.
pmid:34808697.title: Growth hormone for in vitro fertilisation (IVF)
pmid:34808697.finding: Cochrane: in poor responders, growth hormone may raise live birth (OR 1.77, 95% CI 1.17-2.70) but the evidence is very low certainty; about 1.4 more eggs retrieved.

pmid:21422850.authors: Steiner AZ, Herring AH, Kesner JS, et al.
pmid:21422850.title: Antimüllerian hormone as a predictor of natural fecundability in women aged 30-42 years
pmid:21422850.finding: Pilot cohort: AMH <=0.7 ng/mL was associated with lower day-specific natural fecundability (FR 0.38, 95% CI 0.08-0.91).

pmid:29049585.authors: Steiner AZ, Pritchard D, Stanczyk FZ, et al.
pmid:29049585.title: Association Between Biomarkers of Ovarian Reserve and Infertility Among Older Women of Reproductive Age
pmid:29049585.finding: Time to Conceive cohort: low AMH (<0.7 ng/mL) or high FSH did not reduce the chance of natural conception (by 12 cycles, 84% vs 75% with normal AMH).

pmid:32863013.authors: Tiegs AW, Tao X, Zhan Y, et al.
pmid:32863013.title: A multicenter, prospective, blinded, nonselection study evaluating the predictive value of an aneuploid diagnosis using a targeted next-generation sequencing-based preimplantation genetic testing for aneuploidy assay and impact of biopsy
pmid:32863013.finding: Blinded non-selection study: embryos called aneuploid by NGS PGT-A essentially never led to delivery (0% clinical error), and biopsy did not reduce sustained implantation.

pmid:32518919.title: The obligate need for accuracy in reporting preclinical studies relevant to clinical trials: autologous germline mitochondrial supplementation for assisted human reproduction as a case study
pmid:32518919.finding: Review by the laboratory behind AUGMENT: three early uncontrolled studies (104 patients) suggested benefit, a fourth (57 patients) did not; argues safety concerns from a mouse study were misplaced.

pmid:34581729.authors: Davidson KW, Barry MJ, Mangione CM, et al.
pmid:34581729.title: Aspirin Use to Prevent Preeclampsia and Related Morbidity and Mortality: US Preventive Services Task Force Recommendation Statement
pmid:34581729.finding: USPSTF (B): low-dose aspirin 81 mg/day after 12 weeks for people at high risk of pre-eclampsia.

pmid:38682756.authors: Vaidakis D, Papapanou M, Siristatidis CS
pmid:38682756.title: Autologous platelet-rich plasma for assisted reproduction
pmid:38682756.finding: Cochrane: very low-certainty evidence for intrauterine and intraovarian PRP; the only low-risk-of-bias intrauterine trial showed no clear effect on live birth (OR 1.10, 0.38-3.14).

pmid:37336552.authors: van Hoogenhuijze NE, Lahoz Casarramona G, Lensen S, et al.
pmid:37336552.title: Endometrial scratching in women undergoing IVF/ICSI: an individual participant data meta-analysis
pmid:37336552.finding: Individual-participant-data meta-analysis after integrity checks: scratching was associated with higher live birth (OR 1.29, 95% CI 1.02-1.64), but sensitivity analyses were borderline (e.g. OR 1.22, 0.96-1.54) and no subgroup benefited more.

pmid:19432566.authors: Villar J, Purwar M, Merialdi M, et al.
pmid:19432566.title: World Health Organisation multicentre randomised trial of supplementation with vitamins C and E among pregnant women at high risk for pre-eclampsia in populations of low nutritional status from developing countries
pmid:19432566.finding: WHO trial in low-nutrition populations: vitamins C and E did not reduce pre-eclampsia (RR 1.0) or any maternal or perinatal outcome.

pmid:31173348.authors: Wennberg AL, Schildauer K, Brännström M
pmid:31173348.title: Elective oocyte freezing for nonmedical reasons: a 6-year report on utilization and in vitro fertilization results from a Swedish center
pmid:31173348.finding: Swedish elective egg freezing: 15% returned; cumulative live birth/ongoing pregnancy 63% if frozen at 36-37, 26% at 38-39, 0% at 40+.

pmid:34818479.authors: Yan J, Qin Y, Zhao H, et al.
pmid:34818479.title: Live Birth with or without Preimplantation Genetic Testing for Aneuploidy
pmid:34818479.finding: In women with 3+ good blastocysts, cumulative live birth was 77.2% with PGT-A vs 81.8% without (difference -4.6 points); pregnancy loss was 8.7% vs 12.6%.

pmid:26406293.authors: Zarek SM, Mitchell EM, Sjaarda LA, et al.
pmid:26406293.title: Is Anti-Müllerian Hormone Associated With Fecundability? Findings From the EAGeR Trial
pmid:26406293.finding: EAGeR trial cohort: low or high AMH was not associated with fecundability in women with prior losses (FOR 1.13 for low AMH).

pmid:17077236.authors: Chavarro JE, Rich-Edwards JW, Rosner BA, et al.
pmid:17077236.title: Iron intake and risk of ovulatory infertility
pmid:17077236.finding: Women using iron supplements had 40% lower risk of ovulatory infertility (RR 0.60); heme iron was unrelated.

pmid:31152673.authors: Hahn KA, Wesselink AK, Wise LA, et al.
pmid:31152673.title: Iron Consumption Is Not Consistently Associated with Fecundability among North American and Danish Pregnancy Planners
pmid:31152673.n: 4662 pregnancy planners (Denmark n=1693, North America n=2969)
pmid:31152673.finding: Iron intake was not consistently associated with fecundability; supplements helped modestly in North America (FR 1.19) and in women with heavy menses.

pmid:28523093.authors: Nelson KM, Dahlin JL, Bisson J, et al.
pmid:28523093.title: Curcumin May (Not) Defy Science.
pmid:28523093.finding: The authors' follow-up reply to critics of their 2017 review, maintaining that curcumin is an improbable drug lead.

pmid:19735646.authors: Anand P, Nair HB, Sung B, et al.
pmid:19735646.title: Design of curcumin-loaded PLGA nanoparticles formulation with enhanced cellular uptake, and increased bioactivity in vitro and superior bioavailability in vivo.
pmid:19735646.finding: RETRACTED. Aggarwal-lab paper claiming PLGA-nanoparticle curcumin had superior bioactivity and bioavailability; cited here only as an example of the lab's retracted curcumin work.

pmid:20599780.authors: Yadav VR, Prasad S, Kannappan R, et al.
pmid:20599780.title: Cyclodextrin-complexed curcumin exhibits anti-inflammatory and antiproliferative activities superior to those of curcumin through higher cellular uptake.
pmid:20599780.finding: RETRACTED. Aggarwal-lab paper claiming cyclodextrin-complexed curcumin had superior anti-inflammatory activity in cell assays; cited only to flag the retraction.

pmid:31013312.authors: Poolsup N, Suksomboon N, Kurnianta PDM, et al.
pmid:31013312.title: Effects of curcumin on glycemic control and lipid profile in prediabetes and type 2 diabetes mellitus: A systematic review and meta-analysis.
pmid:31013312.finding: RETRACTED. A meta-analysis of curcumin on glycaemic control and lipids in prediabetes/type 2 diabetes; cited only to flag that it was withdrawn and should not be used.

pmid:25817068.authors: Schneider C, Gordon ON, Edwards RL, et al.
pmid:25817068.title: Degradation of Curcumin: From Mechanism to Biological Implications.
pmid:25817068.finding: Curcumin rapidly autoxidizes in vitro into many degradation products, which complicates interpretation of cell and animal data.

pmid:24368738.authors: Heger M, van Golen RF, Broekgaarden M, et al.
pmid:24368738.title: The molecular basis for the pharmacokinetics and pharmacodynamics of curcumin and its metabolites in relation to cancer.
pmid:24368738.finding: Detailed review of curcumin's chemistry (Michael acceptor, metal binding, photochemical instability), poor pharmacokinetics and metabolites in relation to cancer.

pmid:16545122.authors: Lao CD, Ruffin MT 4th, Normolle D, et al.
pmid:16545122.title: Dose escalation of a curcuminoid formulation.
pmid:16545122.finding: Single doses of 0.5-12 g curcumin were well tolerated; no curcumin was detected in serum at 0.5-8 g and only low levels in two subjects at 10-12 g.

pmid:15501961.authors: Sharma RA, Euden SA, Platton SL, et al.
pmid:15501961.title: Phase I clinical trial of oral curcumin: biomarkers of systemic activity and compliance.
pmid:15501961.finding: Phase I, 0.45-3.6 g/day for up to 4 months: no dose-limiting toxicity; curcumin and conjugates in plasma only in the ~10 nmol/L range; 3.6 g lowered ex vivo inducible PGE2 in leukocytes.

pmid:11712783.authors: Cheng AL, Hsu CH, Lin JK, et al.
pmid:11712783.title: Phase I clinical trial of curcumin, a chemopreventive agent, in patients with high-risk or pre-malignant lesions.
pmid:11712783.finding: Phase I dose escalation from 0.5 to 12 g/day for 3 months found no toxicity up to 8 g/day for 3 months (higher doses were too bulky to take); mean peak serum curcumin was 0.51, 0.63 and 1.77 uM after 4, 6 and 8 g.

pmid:14997198.authors: Garcea G, Jones DJ, Singh R, et al.
pmid:14997198.title: Detection of curcumin and its metabolites in hepatic tissue and portal blood of patients following oral administration.
pmid:14997198.finding: 0.45-3.6 g/day curcumin for 1 week gave only low nanomolar parent and conjugates in portal and peripheral blood and no curcumin in liver tissue; oxidative DNA adducts in liver were not reduced.

pmid:31962379.authors: Luis PB, Kunihiro AG, Funk JL, et al.
pmid:31962379.title: Incomplete Hydrolysis of Curcumin Conjugates by β-Glucuronidase: Detection of Complex Conjugates in Plasma.
pmid:31962379.finding: Beta-glucuronidase only partly hydrolyses curcumin conjugates in plasma (complex sulfate conjugates remain), so 'total curcumin' assays differ by method and are hard to compare.

pmid:21603867.authors: Kanai M, Imaizumi A, Otsuka Y, et al.
pmid:21603867.title: Dose-escalation and pharmacokinetic study of nanoparticle curcumin, a potential anticancer agent with improved bioavailability, in healthy human volunteers.
pmid:21603867.finding: Theracurmin nanoparticle curcumin at 150 and 210 mg gave mean plasma Cmax of 189 and 275 ng/mL, without saturating absorption.

pmid:12570874.authors: Balogun E, Hoque M, Gong P, et al.
pmid:12570874.title: Curcumin activates the haem oxygenase-1 gene via regulation of Nrf2 and the antioxidant-responsive element.
pmid:12570874.finding: In renal epithelial cells curcumin activates Nrf2 and induces haem oxygenase-1 through the antioxidant response element.

pmid:30860383.authors: Cheng D, Li W, Wang L, et al.
pmid:30860383.title: Pharmacokinetics, Pharmacodynamics, and PKPD Modeling of Curcumin in Regulating Antioxidant and Epigenetic Gene Expression in Healthy Human Volunteers.
pmid:30860383.finding: After a single 4 g dose, parent curcumin was undetectable in plasma; curcumin glucuronide appeared and leukocyte NRF2/HO-1/NQO1 and HDAC mRNA changes were modelled as responses.

pmid:18841446.authors: Cheung KL, Khor TO, Kong AN
pmid:18841446.title: Synergistic effect of combination of phenethyl isothiocyanate and sulforaphane or curcumin and sulforaphane in the inhibition of inflammation.
pmid:18841446.finding: In cell culture, curcumin plus sulforaphane suppressed inflammatory markers (NO, PGE2, TNF, IL-1) synergistically, with synergistic HO-1 and NQO1 induction; no human data.

pmid:33172016.authors: Jakubczyk K, Drużga A, Katarzyna J, et al.
pmid:33172016.title: Antioxidant Potential of Curcumin-A Meta-Analysis of Randomized Clinical Trials.
pmid:33172016.finding: Curcumin (mean 645 mg/day, ~67 days) raised total antioxidant capacity (SMD 2.70) and non-significantly lowered MDA (SMD -1.58, p=0.086); only four trials qualified.

pmid:38892660.title: Is Curcumin Intake Really Effective for Chronic Inflammatory Metabolic Disease? A Review of Meta-Analyses of Randomized Controlled Trials.
pmid:38892660.finding: Review of meta-analyses: CRP fell in 7 of 10, IL-6 in 5 of 8, MDA in 5 of 6, fasting glucose in 14 of 15 and HOMA-IR in 12 of 12 meta-analyses of curcumin RCTs.

pmid:25618800.authors: Panahi Y, Hosseini MS, Khalili N, et al.
pmid:25618800.title: Antioxidant and anti-inflammatory effects of curcuminoid-piperine combination in subjects with metabolic syndrome: A randomized controlled trial and an updated meta-analysis.
pmid:25618800.finding: 1 g/day curcuminoids plus 10 mg piperine for 8 weeks raised SOD and lowered MDA and CRP versus placebo (Iranian trial, with an accompanying CRP meta-analysis).

pmid:29018060.authors: Liu X, Machado GC, Eyles JP, et al.
pmid:29018060.title: Dietary supplements for treating osteoarthritis: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
pmid:29018060.finding: Curcuma longa extract and curcumin were among 7 supplements with large short-term effects on OA pain, but no supplement showed clinically important long-term pain relief.

pmid:25308211.authors: Nakagawa Y, Mukai S, Yamada S, et al.
pmid:25308211.title: Short-term effects of highly-bioavailable curcumin for treating knee osteoarthritis: a randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled prospective study.
pmid:25308211.finding: Theracurmin (180 mg/day curcumin) for 8 weeks lowered knee-pain VAS versus placebo (except in mild cases) and reduced celecoxib use; developer-affiliated study.

pmid:21194249.authors: Belcaro G, Cesarone MR, Dugall M, et al.
pmid:21194249.title: Efficacy and safety of Meriva®, a curcumin-phosphatidylcholine complex, during extended administration in osteoarthritis patients.
pmid:21194249.finding: Meriva for 8 months improved WOMAC scores and inflammatory markers versus a control group; open, non-randomised design.

pmid:38213188.authors: Vajdi M, Hassanizadeh S, Hassanizadeh R, et al.
pmid:38213188.title: Curcumin supplementation effect on liver enzymes in patients with nonalcoholic fatty liver disease: a GRADE-assessed systematic review and dose-response meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials.
pmid:38213188.finding: In NAFLD, curcumin lowered ALT (-4.1 U/L) and AST (-3.3 U/L) but not ALP; curcumin plus piperine had no significant effect on ALT.

pmid:38232906.authors: Ebrahimzadeh A, Mohseni S, Safargar M, et al.
pmid:38232906.title: Curcumin effects on glycaemic indices, lipid profile, blood pressure, inflammatory markers and anthropometric measurements of non-alcoholic fatty liver disease patients: A systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized clinical trials.
pmid:38232906.finding: In NAFLD, curcumin 50-3000 mg/day lowered fasting glucose, HOMA-IR, TG, TC, LDL and weight but not HbA1c, CRP, TNF-a or blood pressure; authors flag bias and possible adulteration.

pmid:22773702.authors: Chuengsamarn S, Rattanamongkolgul S, Luechapudiporn R, et al.
pmid:22773702.title: Curcumin extract for prevention of type 2 diabetes.
pmid:22773702.finding: 9 months of curcumin extract: 0% vs 16.4% progressed to type 2 diabetes, with better HOMA-beta and HOMA-IR; an unusually large single-trial effect not yet replicated.

pmid:31871950.authors: Funamoto M, Shimizu K, Sunagawa Y, et al.
pmid:31871950.title: Effects of Highly Absorbable Curcumin in Patients with Impaired Glucose Tolerance and Non-Insulin-Dependent Diabetes Mellitus.
pmid:31871950.finding: Theracurmin 180 mg/day for 6 months did not change HbA1c (primary endpoint); oxidised LDL rose in the placebo group but not with curcumin.

pmid:33514002.authors: Altobelli E, Angeletti PM, Marziliano C, et al.
pmid:33514002.title: Potential Therapeutic Effects of Curcumin on Glycemic and Lipid Profile in Uncomplicated Type 2 Diabetes-A Meta-Analysis of Randomized Controlled Trial.
pmid:33514002.finding: Curcumin did not significantly lower fasting glucose but did reduce HbA1c, HOMA and LDL in uncomplicated type 2 diabetes.

pmid:37230418.authors: Dehzad MJ, Ghalandari H, Amini MR, et al.
pmid:37230418.title: Effects of curcumin/turmeric supplementation on lipid profile: A GRADE-assessed systematic review and dose-response meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials.
pmid:37230418.finding: Turmeric/curcumin lowered TC (-4.0 mg/dL), TG (-6.7), LDL (-4.9) and raised HDL (+1.8) but did not change ApoA or ApoB; GRADE certainty low to very low.

pmid:24139527.title: A systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials investigating the effects of curcumin on blood lipid levels.
pmid:24139527.finding: Early meta-analysis found no significant effect of curcumin on any blood lipid.

pmid:28236605.authors: Ng QX, Koh SSH, Chan HW, et al.
pmid:28236605.title: Clinical Use of Curcumin in Depression: A Meta-Analysis.
pmid:28236605.finding: Curcumin improved Hamilton depression scores versus placebo (SMD -0.34); few, small trials.

pmid:42472817.authors: Musazadeh V, Faghfouri AH, Falahatzadeh M, et al.
pmid:42472817.title: Efficacy of curcumin in depression: A grade-assessed systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials.
pmid:42472817.finding: Curcumin improved depression (SMD -0.76) and depressive symptoms (SMD -0.53) but heterogeneity was very high (I2 >85%) and the effect was fragile in sensitivity analysis.

pmid:40314175.authors: Cheng YC, Huang WL, Chen WY, et al.
pmid:40314175.title: Comparative efficacy and tolerability of nutraceuticals for depressive disorder: A systematic review and network meta-analysis.
pmid:40314175.finding: Network meta-analysis: curcumin added to antidepressants improved symptoms (SMD 1.03), while curcumin monotherapy versus antidepressants was not significant (CI crossed zero).

pmid:27102361.authors: Rainey-Smith SR, Brown BM, Sohrabi HR, et al.
pmid:27102361.title: Curcumin and cognition: a randomised, placebo-controlled, double-blind study of community-dwelling older adults.
pmid:27102361.finding: Biocurcumax 1500 mg/day for 12 months: no difference on most cognitive measures; one MoCA interaction driven by decline in the placebo group at 6 months.

pmid:25277322.authors: Cox KH, Pipingas A, Scholey AB
pmid:25277322.title: Investigation of the effects of solid lipid curcumin on cognition and mood in a healthy older population.
pmid:25277322.finding: Longvida solid-lipid curcumin 400 mg improved attention and working memory acutely and after 4 weeks, and lowered total and LDL cholesterol.

pmid:40308636.authors: Wang W, Zhao R, Liu B, et al.
pmid:40308636.title: The effect of curcumin supplementation on cognitive function: an updated systematic review and meta-analysis.
pmid:40308636.finding: Curcumin improved global cognition (SMD 0.82) only in trials >=24 weeks, in people >=60 or in Asian populations; small evidence base.

pmid:39008500.authors: Liu X, Lin L, Hu G
pmid:39008500.title: Meta-analysis of the effect of curcumin supplementation on skeletal muscle damage status.
pmid:39008500.finding: Curcumin reduced muscle soreness (MD -0.61), CK (MD -137) and IL-6 and improved range of motion after exercise.

pmid:36125053.authors: Bańkowski S, Petr M, Rozpara M, et al.
pmid:36125053.title: Effect of 6-week curcumin supplementation on aerobic capacity, antioxidant status and sirtuin 3 level in middle-aged amateur long-distance runners.
pmid:36125053.finding: 2 g/day curcumin for 6 weeks did not change VO2max, antioxidant enzymes, oxidative-stress or muscle-damage markers; resting SIRT3 rose.

pmid:26278015.authors: Ray Hamidie RD, Yamada T, Ishizawa R, et al.
pmid:26278015.title: Curcumin treatment enhances the effect of exercise on mitochondrial biogenesis in skeletal muscle by increasing cAMP levels.
pmid:26278015.finding: In rats, injected curcumin plus endurance training increased muscle mitochondrial biogenesis markers more than training alone (via cAMP/PKA, AMPK/PGC-1a).

pmid:21372035.authors: Carroll RE, Benya RV, Turgeon DK, et al.
pmid:21372035.title: Phase IIa clinical trial of curcumin for the prevention of colorectal neoplasia.
pmid:21372035.finding: Curcumin 4 g/day (not 2 g) for 30 days cut aberrant crypt foci by 40%, but did not change PGE2, 5-HETE or Ki-67; non-randomised.

pmid:31132111.authors: Howells LM, Iwuji COO, Irving GRB, et al.
pmid:31132111.title: Curcumin Combined with FOLFOX Chemotherapy Is Safe and Tolerable in Patients with Metastatic Colorectal Cancer in a Randomized Phase IIa Trial.
pmid:31132111.finding: Adding 2 g/day curcumin to FOLFOX was safe; exploratory overall-survival HR 0.34 in an open-label phase IIa trial too small for efficacy conclusions.

pmid:30671976.authors: Choi YH, Han DH, Kim SW, et al.
pmid:30671976.title: A randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial to evaluate the role of curcumin in prostate cancer patients with intermittent androgen deprivation.
pmid:30671976.n: 97 men with prostate cancer on intermittent ADT
pmid:30671976.finding: Curcumin 1440 mg/day for 6 months did not lengthen the off-treatment interval versus placebo.

pmid:18628464.authors: Dhillon N, Aggarwal BB, Newman RA, et al.
pmid:18628464.title: Phase II trial of curcumin in patients with advanced pancreatic cancer.
pmid:18628464.finding: 8 g/day curcumin: low circulating conjugates, 2 of 21 evaluable patients showed biological activity; uncontrolled phase II.

pmid:28734960.authors: Bahramsoltani R, Rahimi R, Farzaei MH
pmid:28734960.title: Pharmacokinetic interactions of curcuminoids with conventional drugs: A review.
pmid:28734960.finding: Curcumin inhibits CYP isoenzymes and P-glycoprotein and alters drug pharmacokinetics in vitro and in animals; human interaction data are sparse.

pmid:23807811.authors: Liu AC, Zhao LX, Lou HX
pmid:23807811.title: Curcumin alters the pharmacokinetics of warfarin and clopidogrel in Wistar rats but has no effect on anticoagulation or antiplatelet aggregation.
pmid:23807811.finding: In rats, 100 mg/kg curcumin raised warfarin and clopidogrel exposure (~1.5-1.8-fold) without changing prothrombin time or platelet aggregation.

deep-curcumin:cur-pubmed-retractions.title: PubMed searches 'Aggarwal BB[au] AND retracted publication[pt]' and 'curcumin AND retracted publication[pt]', run 2026-10-01 via NCBI E-utilities.
deep-curcumin:cur-pubmed-retractions.finding: Returned 27 retracted publications with BB Aggarwal as author and 162 retracted publications mentioning curcumin.

pmid:26654757.title: Mitohormesis in exercise training.
pmid:26654757.finding: Reviews mitohormesis in exercise; notes that studies directly linking mitochondrial retrograde signals to human training responses are still lacking, with ROS the main candidate signal.

pmid:28371751.authors: Cobley JN, Close GL, Bailey DM, et al.
pmid:28371751.title: Exercise redox biochemistry: Conceptual, methodological and technical recommendations.
pmid:28371751.finding: Methods paper warning that many exercise redox studies use outdated assays (e.g. TBARS), ignore repair and chemical heterogeneity, and should use multiple validated biomarkers.

pmid:6061736.authors: Owen OE, Morgan AP, Kemp HG, et al.
pmid:6061736.title: Brain metabolism during fasting.
pmid:6061736.finding: Cerebral catheterisation after 5-6 weeks of starvation showed beta-hydroxybutyrate and acetoacetate had replaced glucose as the brain's predominant fuel.

pmid:1948033.authors: Rothman DL, Magnusson I, Katz LD, et al.
pmid:1948033.title: Quantitation of hepatic glycogenolysis and gluconeogenesis in fasting humans with 13C NMR.
pmid:1948033.finding: Serial liver 13C NMR over a 68-h fast: gluconeogenesis supplied 64% of glucose output in the first 22 h, 82% over the next 14 h and 96% over the following 18 h as liver glycogen ran down.

pmid:8755648.authors: Landau BR, Wahren J, Chandramouli V, et al.
pmid:8755648.title: Contributions of gluconeogenesis to glucose production in the fasted state.
pmid:8755648.finding: Gluconeogenesis contributed ~47% of glucose production after 14 h, 67% after 22 h and 93% after 42 h of fasting.

pmid:8238506.authors: Klein S, Sakurai Y, Romijn JA, et al.
pmid:8238506.title: Progressive alterations in lipid and glucose metabolism during short-term fasting in young adult men.
pmid:8238506.finding: Across 12-72 h of fasting, lipolysis doubled (60% of the rise by 24 h, largest step at 18-24 h), glucose fell ~25% (5.6 to 4.1 mmol/L) and insulin halved, with 70% of the insulin decline in the first 24 h.

pmid:3127426.authors: Ho KY, Veldhuis JD, Johnson ML, et al.
pmid:3127426.title: Fasting enhances growth hormone secretion and amplifies the complex rhythms of growth hormone secretion in man.
pmid:3127426.finding: By day 5 of a fast, 24-h integrated growth hormone rose ~3-fold (2.82 to 8.75 ug.min/mL) with more frequent, larger pulses.

pmid:30135314.authors: Steinhauser ML, Olenchock BA, O'Keefe J, et al.
pmid:30135314.title: The circulating metabolome of human starvation.
pmid:30135314.finding: Plasma metabolomics during a 10-day zero-calorie fast showed early consumption of gluconeogenic amino acids, then a surge of fatty acids marking the shift to lipid fuel, possibly driven by falling leptin.

pmid:30696848.authors: Teruya T, Chaleckis R, Takada J, et al.
pmid:30696848.title: Diverse metabolic reactions activated during 58-hr fasting are revealed by non-targeted metabolomic analysis of human blood.
pmid:30696848.finding: Non-targeted blood metabolomics during 34-58 h fasts found 44 metabolites up 1.5-60-fold, including pentose-phosphate and TCA-cycle compounds; authors propose antioxidant (NADPH) demand as a principal fasting response.

pmid:23657581.authors: Buffet A, Vezzosi D, Maiza JC, et al.
pmid:23657581.title: Increased plasma β-hydroxybutyrate levels during the fasting test in patients with endogenous hyperinsulinaemic hypoglycaemia.
pmid:23657581.finding: People without insulinoma undergoing a supervised 72-h fast reached a median plasma beta-hydroxybutyrate of ~6.1 mmol/L at the end of the test, showing how high fasting ketosis can climb.

pmid:20534972.authors: Alirezaei M, Kemball CC, Flynn CT, et al.
pmid:20534972.title: Short-term fasting induces profound neuronal autophagy.
pmid:20534972.finding: In mice, short-term (24-48 h) food restriction markedly increased autophagosomes in cortical neurons and Purkinje cells; the main source of the popular 'autophagy at 24-48 h' claim.

pmid:28059587.authors: Pietrocola F, Demont Y, Castoldi F, et al.
pmid:28059587.title: Metabolic effects of fasting on human and mouse blood in vivo.
pmid:28059587.finding: Fasting up to 4 days in humans changed the plasma metabolome and reduced leukocyte protein acetylation, but increased autophagic flux was detectable only in neutrophils and only with ex vivo protease inhibition.

pmid:30161009.authors: Dethlefsen MM, Bertholdt L, Gudiksen A, et al.
pmid:30161009.title: Training state and skeletal muscle autophagy in response to 36 h of fasting.
pmid:30161009.finding: Muscle biopsies at 2-36 h of fasting showed only modest changes in autophagy markers (LC3, p62), in untrained men only; training status altered the response.

pmid:40345145.authors: Bensalem J, Teong XT, Hattersley KJ, et al.
pmid:40345145.title: Intermittent time-restricted eating may increase autophagic flux in humans: an exploratory analysis.
pmid:40345145.finding: PBMC LC3B-II autophagic flux differed between intermittent fasting plus TRE and standard care at 6 months (post hoc, P = 0.04), partly because flux fell in controls; CR vs control was not significant.

pmid:30172870.authors: Bagherniya M, Butler AE, Barreto GE, et al.
pmid:30172870.title: The effect of fasting or calorie restriction on autophagy induction: A review of the literature.
pmid:30172870.finding: Review concluding fasting and CR are potent autophagy inducers, with the evidence coming overwhelmingly from cell and animal studies; human data are sparse.

pmid:23150812.authors: Faris MA, Hussein RN, Al-Kurd RA, et al.
pmid:23150812.title: Impact of ramadan intermittent fasting on oxidative stress measured by urinary 15-f(2t)-isoprostane.
pmid:23150812.finding: Urinary 15-F2t-isoprostane rose by week 3 of Ramadan alongside gains in weight and body fat, suggesting the oxidative effect followed weight change, not fasting per se.

pmid:19011280.authors: Ibrahim WH, Habib HM, Jarrar AH, et al.
pmid:19011280.title: Effect of Ramadan fasting on markers of oxidative stress and serum biochemical markers of cellular damage in healthy subjects.
pmid:19011280.finding: Across Ramadan, erythrocyte MDA fell slightly while plasma protein carbonyls, glutathione, GPx, catalase and serum MDA were unchanged.

pmid:31356832.authors: Madkour MI, T El-Serafi A, Jahrami HA, et al.
pmid:31356832.title: Ramadan diurnal intermittent fasting modulates SOD2, TFAM, Nrf2, and sirtuins (SIRT1, SIRT3) gene expressions in subjects with overweight and obesity.
pmid:31356832.finding: After Ramadan, expression of TFAM, SOD2 and Nrf2 rose (by 90%, 54% and 412%) while SIRT3 fell 62%; gene expression only, no damage markers.

pmid:30813495.authors: Fernando HA, Zibellini J, Harris RA, et al.
pmid:30813495.title: Effect of Ramadan Fasting on Weight and Body Composition in Healthy Non-Athlete Adults: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
pmid:30813495.finding: Ramadan fasting produced small, transient weight and fat losses (fat % fell only in people with overweight), with some fat-free mass loss, largely regained 2-5 weeks later.

pmid:28087222.authors: Friedli N, Stanga Z, Sobotka L, et al.
pmid:28087222.title: Revisiting the refeeding syndrome: Results of a systematic review.
pmid:28087222.finding: Systematic review: refeeding syndrome definitions vary widely (incidence 0-80%), but it occurs mostly within 72 h of restarting nutrition.

pmid:1647144.authors: Sichieri R, Everhart JE, Roth H
pmid:1647144.title: A prospective study of hospitalization with gallstone disease among women: role of dietary factors, fasting period, and dieting.
pmid:1647144.finding: Over 10 years, risk of hospitalisation with gallstone disease rose with longer overnight fasting periods and with dieting; fibre was mildly protective.

pmid:1587196.authors: Yang H, Petersen GM, Roth MP, et al.
pmid:1587196.title: Risk factors for gallstone formation during rapid loss of weight.
pmid:1587196.finding: 10.9% developed gallstones within 16 weeks of rapid weight loss on a very-low-calorie diet; higher BMI and greater BMI loss raised risk.

pmid:28347497.authors: Hassanein M, Al-Arouj M, Hamdy O, et al.
pmid:28347497.title: Diabetes and Ramadan: Practical guidelines.
pmid:28347497.finding: IDF-DAR practical guidelines for fasting with diabetes: risk stratification, nutrition advice and medication adjustment for insulin and sulfonylureas.

pmid:36368052.authors: Ganson KT, Cuccolo K, Hallward L, et al.
pmid:36368052.title: Intermittent fasting: Describing engagement and associations with eating disorder behaviors and psychopathology among Canadian adolescents and young adults.
pmid:36368052.finding: Almost half of Canadian young people reported intermittent fasting in the past year, and it was associated with eating-disorder behaviours and psychopathology, most consistently in women.

pmid:29315892.authors: Aird TP, Davies RW, Carson BP
pmid:29315892.title: Effects of fasted vs fed-state exercise on performance and post-exercise metabolism: A systematic review and meta-analysis.
pmid:29315892.finding: Pre-exercise feeding improved prolonged aerobic performance but not shorter exercise; fasted exercise raised post-exercise fatty acids and muscle signalling linked to mitochondrial adaptation.

pmid:31628477.authors: Edinburgh RM, Bradley HE, Abdullah NF, et al.
pmid:31628477.title: Lipid Metabolism Links Nutrient-Exercise Timing to Insulin Sensitivity in Men Classified as Overweight or Obese.
pmid:31628477.finding: 6 weeks of cycling performed before vs after carbohydrate intake lowered postprandial insulin and improved oral glucose insulin sensitivity, linked to greater lipid use during exercise.

pmid:31832984.authors: Faris MAE, Jahrami HA, Alhayki FA, et al.
pmid:31832984.title: Effect of diurnal fasting on sleep during Ramadan: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
pmid:31832984.finding: During Ramadan total sleep time fell from ~7.2 to ~6.4 h/night with a negligible change in daytime sleepiness.

pmid:40560588.authors: Clavero-Jimeno A, Dote-Montero M, Migueles JH, et al.
pmid:40560588.title: Time-Restricted Eating and Sleep, Mood, and Quality of Life in Adults With Overweight or Obesity: A Secondary Analysis of a Randomized Clinical Trial.
pmid:40560588.finding: 12 weeks of early, late or self-selected 8-h TRE did not change sleep, mood or quality of life vs usual care.

pmid:1677062.title: Prevention of neural tube defects: results of the Medical Research Council Vitamin Study. MRC Vitamin Study Research Group
pmid:1677062.finding: MRC Vitamin Study: periconceptional folic acid (4 mg) prevented 72% of recurrent neural tube defects (RR 0.28); other vitamins had no protective effect.

pmid:24518810.authors: Pineles BL, Park E, Samet JM
pmid:24518810.title: Systematic review and meta-analysis of miscarriage and maternal exposure to tobacco smoke during pregnancy
pmid:24518810.finding: Active smoking raised miscarriage risk (RR 1.23; 1.32 when smoking was in the index pregnancy), about 1% per cigarette per day; secondhand smoke +11%.

pmid:31194258.authors: Sundermann AC, Zhao S, Young CL, et al.
pmid:31194258.title: Alcohol Use in Pregnancy and Miscarriage: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis
pmid:31194258.finding: Any alcohol in pregnancy raised miscarriage risk (OR 1.19); each extra drink per week up to 5 added about 6%.

pmid:1757519.authors: Thonneau P, Marchand S, Tallec A, et al.
pmid:1757519.title: Incidence and main causes of infertility in a resident population (1,850,000) of three French regions (1988-1989)
pmid:1757519.finding: French population survey: the woman alone explained infertility in one-third of couples, the man alone in one-fifth, and both partners in 39%; 8% unexplained.

pmid:25928197.authors: Agarwal A, Mulgund A, Hamada A, et al.
pmid:25928197.title: A unique view on male infertility around the globe
pmid:25928197.finding: Global estimate: male factor accounts for 20-70% of infertility depending on region; at least 30 million men are infertile.

pmid:32115183.authors: Practice Committee of the American Society for Reproductive Medicine
pmid:32115183.title: Definitions of infertility and recurrent pregnancy loss: a committee opinion
pmid:32115183.finding: ASRM: infertility is failure to conceive after 12 months of regular unprotected intercourse, with evaluation after 6 months for women over 35 and earlier when history warrants.

pmid:34607703.authors: Practice Committee of the American Society for Reproductive Medicine
pmid:34607703.title: Fertility evaluation of infertile women: a committee opinion
pmid:34607703.finding: ASRM: systematic, expeditious evaluation of infertile women, least invasive tests first; evaluation should proceed in parallel with the male partner.

pmid:37599566.authors: ESHRE Guideline Group on Unexplained Infertility
pmid:37599566.title: Evidence-based guideline: unexplained infertility
pmid:37599566.finding: ESHRE unexplained infertility guideline: basic work-up for both partners; first-line treatment IUI with ovarian stimulation; no recommendation backed by high-quality evidence.

pmid:30259705.authors: Esbert M, Pacheco A, Soares SR, et al.
pmid:30259705.title: High sperm DNA fragmentation delays human embryo kinetics when oocytes from young and healthy donors are microinjected
pmid:30259705.finding: High SDF (>20%) slowed embryo cell divisions when young donor eggs were used, consistent with time spent on DNA repair.

deep-fertility-extras:fer-hfea2026.title: Treatment add-ons with limited evidence (HFEA add-ons rating list)
deep-fertility-extras:fer-hfea2026.finding: HFEA traffic-light ratings for 'chances of having a baby' (page reviewed 28 Sep 2026; ratings set by SCAAC): yellow/amber (unclear) for endometrial scratching, hyaluronate-enriched transfer medium and elective freeze-all; grey (insufficient evidence) for assisted hatching, androgens, intralipids, IMSI, intrauterine culture, microbiome testing and SDF-guided treatments; black (no effect) for time-lapse imaging and PICSI; red (no benefit and/or safety concerns) for endometrial receptivity testing, IVIG, steroids, PRP and PGT-A (PGT-A rated green for reducing miscarriage). No green rating for live birth.

deep-fertility-extras:fer-hfea2026sdf.title: Sperm DNA fragmentation: treatment add-on rating
deep-fertility-extras:fer-hfea2026sdf.finding: After SDF testing: antioxidants and sperm selection (DGC/MACS with ICSI or PICSI) rated grey (insufficient evidence) for male factor and recurrent pregnancy loss; testicular sperm (TESE/TESA) with ICSI rated red for male factor (insufficient evidence plus surgical risk). Reviewed 24 Sep 2026.

deep-fertility-extras:fer-hfea2026prp.title: Platelet-rich plasma (PRP): treatment add-on rating
deep-fertility-extras:fer-hfea2026prp.finding: Intraovarian PRP for poor/diminished ovarian reserve and intrauterine PRP for thin endometrium, recurrent implantation failure, Asherman's syndrome and recurrent pregnancy loss all rated red (safety concerns, no moderate/high-quality evidence); not rated for most patients because there is no medical reason to offer it. Reviewed 27 Feb 2026.

deep-fertility-extras:fer-hfea2025androg.title: Androgen supplementation (DHEA and testosterone): treatment add-on rating
deep-fertility-extras:fer-hfea2025androg.finding: DHEA rated black (no effect) on eggs retrieved and live birth in poor responders and grey elsewhere; testosterone rated grey for all groups. Reviewed 9 Jun 2025.

pmid:18069785.authors: Miglio C, Chiavaro E, Visconti A, et al.
pmid:18069785.title: Effects of different cooking methods on nutritional and physicochemical characteristics of selected vegetables.
pmid:18069785.finding: Boiling and steaming preserved carotenoids better than frying; frying retained fewer antioxidants; cooking softened the matrix and raised measured antioxidant capacity.

pmid:19650196.authors: Yuan GF, Sun B, Yuan J, et al.
pmid:19650196.title: Effects of different cooking methods on health-promoting compounds of broccoli.
pmid:19650196.finding: Steaming broccoli best retained vitamin C, chlorophyll and glucosinolates; stir-frying and stir-fry/boiling caused the largest losses.

pmid:17011103.title: Effect of storage, processing and cooking on glucosinolate content of Brassica vegetables.
pmid:17011103.finding: Steaming, microwaving and stir-frying did not significantly reduce Brassica glucosinolates, whereas boiling leached ~90% of losses into the water; fine shredding then standing lost up to 75% in 6 h.

pmid:24227349.authors: Palermo M, Pellegrini N, Fogliano V
pmid:24227349.title: The effect of cooking on the phytochemical content of vegetables.
pmid:24227349.finding: Steaming generally preserves phenols and glucosinolates best; carotenoids often become more extractable after more severe heating.

pmid:11982434.authors: Dewanto V, Wu X, Adom KK, et al.
pmid:11982434.title: Thermal processing enhances the nutritional value of tomatoes by increasing total antioxidant activity.
pmid:11982434.finding: Heating tomatoes at 88 °C for 2-30 min raised bioaccessible lycopene and total antioxidant activity while vitamin C fell.

pmid:30263756.authors: Lee S, Choi Y, Jeong HS, et al.
